tracks.name: Building Heat Treatment Plants in Odoo: Automating ETO Manufacturing with 20,000 BoMs
tracks.speaker_line: Nadja Planic, Head of Manufacturing ERP Consulting at much. Consulting
tracks.description_html:
In Engineering-to-Order (ETO) manufacturing, the transition from design to production often breaks down when teams rely on disconnected spreadsheets. Kohnle, a manufacturer of industrial heat treatment plants, experienced this firsthand. They managed a large catalog of 45,000 products and 20,000 Bills of Materials (BoMs) using manual cost calculations in Excel and static quotes in Word. These media breaks forced the team into time-consuming data re-entry, causing procurement errors that directly threatened project timelines.

To resolve this, we consolidated their entire engineering and manufacturing logic into Odoo Enterprise, utilizing Analytical Accounting and PLM to enforce a rigid "Release-to-Manufacture" process and cost control.

Additionally, with automatic task creation and bidirectional data synchronization from Manufacturing Orders into the Project App, we transformed static manufacturing data into dynamic project milestones. This architecture allows Kohnle to manage dependencies and resource planning within the Odoo Gantt view, providing a real-time overview of their complex engineering projects.

Key Points of the Talk:

- Leaving Spreadsheets Behind: How Kohnle moved 45,000 products and 20,000 BoMs from fragmented media into one unified system.
- Structuring the Engineering Handover: How we implemented Odoo BoM releases to create a clear process for sending designs to production.
- Connecting Production to Planning: Automatically creating Project Tasks from Manufacturing Orders to keep long-term schedules up to date.
- Building Digital Guardrails: Enforcing data integrity via granular access rights during cross-department handovers.
- Closing the Gaps: Eliminating manual media breaks between cost calculation, quoting, and production execution.

Key Learnings:

- How to bridge the functional gap between PLM engineering and MRP production.
- How to automate project-based manufacturing using Odoo’s native task-sync logic.
- How to manage large-scale data migrations without losing BoM hierarchy.
- How to configure Odoo Enterprise to handle complex ETO timeline dependencies.

Target Audience:

- Operations Managers and CTOs in Engineering/Manufacturing.
- Project Leads managing complex ETO cycles in Odoo Enterprise.
- Functional Consultants specialized in PLM and MRP integrations.

tracks.name: From Salesforce to Odoo: Rebuilding a Healthcare Platform for Scale and Cost Efficiency
tracks.speaker_line: Faisal Basar, CEO at Bista Solutions
tracks.description_html:
This talk explores how MenMD, a U.S.-based digital healthcare platform, successfully transitioned from Salesforce to a fully customized Odoo ERP solution, implemented by Bista Solutions Inc.. Facing rising software costs, fragmented systems, and an urgent contract renewal deadline, MenMD needed to replace Salesforce while improving scalability, operational control, and compliance. The result was a unified platform that reduced overall software costs by approximately 75% while supporting continued growth.

Attendees will gain insight into how Odoo was tailored to support complex healthcare workflows, including HIPAA-compliant architecture, patient and doctor portals, prescription management, appointment scheduling, and subscription-based services. The session will also highlight key challenges such as securely migrating sensitive patient data, handling edge cases in prescription workflows, and building custom payment and access control processes.

Key learnings include how to replace a costly CRM with a full ERP, strategies for managing compliance and data security in healthcare environments, and how to execute a large-scale implementation under strict time constraints. This talk is ideal for healthcare providers, digital health platforms, and operations and IT leaders looking to reduce costs, unify systems, and scale efficiently with Odoo.

tracks.name: Stop Writing AI Prompts by Hand: Building a Self-Fixing Native AI Loop in Odoo 19
tracks.speaker_line: Mike Schulz, Senior Expert ERP Consultant at much. Consulting
tracks.description_html:
Static AI prompts lose accuracy quickly as new business edge cases pop up, forcing admins to constantly rewrite them. When routing Helpdesk tickets or scoring CRM leads, the AI often guesses wrong. Users fix these mistakes daily, but the system forgets the corrections, forcing people to fix the same errors over and over.

To solve this, we built a two-agent system that learns from its mistakes, using only standard Odoo Enterprise v19 AI features. We set this up entirely using Odoo Studio and server actions—no custom Python code required. When a user changes an AI-generated field—like fixing a wrong ticket priority—a second background AI immediately notices the change. This second AI looks at why the user made the change and automatically rewrites the first AI's instructions so it gets it right the next time.

By feeding human corrections directly back into the system, we completely stopped writing AI prompts by hand in our testing environment. This setup matches AI outputs directly to real human actions, allowing CRM and Helpdesk automation to run without constant admin upkeep.

Key Points of this Talk:

- Set up two-part AI loops using built-in Odoo Enterprise v19 AI functions.
- Record manual field changes to trigger background AI updates.
- Use Odoo Studio to automate AI prompt changes without custom Python code.
- Build server actions to update AI prompts automatically on the fly.
- Apply self-correcting loops to CRM lead scoring and Helpdesk ticket routing.

Key Learnings:

- How to build an AI loop that fixes itself using Odoo Enterprise v19 features.
- How to use manual field edits to train a background AI assistant.
- How to stop writing AI prompts by hand using Odoo server actions.
- How to use Odoo Studio to manage multi-step AI setups.

Target Audience:

Business Leaders, System Administrators, and Implementation Managers using Odoo Enterprise v19+

tracks.name: How do we know Odoo AI workflows still work?
tracks.speaker_line: Andrzej Pietrusiak, Software developer at Odoo
tracks.description_html:
You shipped an AI feature. It works today. But what happens when the prompt changes, the model evolves, the business logic moves, or user expectations become clearer? Are you supposed to manually open every flow and check whether the AI still behaves correctly?

This talk presents a practical approach to evaluating AI workflows in Odoo through repeatable scenarios and lightweight benchmarks. We will look at how to run AI flows automatically, compare results over time, catch regressions faster, all that helps developers improve AI features with more confidence.

The goal is simple: make AI features easier to maintain.

tracks.name: From Odoo to Everywhere : Selling Across Marketplaces with Shoppingfeed
tracks.speaker_line: Arnaud Percy, CEO at tsc - The Service Company SRL
tracks.description_html:
Many companies using Odoo want to expand their online sales beyond their own webshop and start selling on marketplaces such as la fnac, Bol.com, décathlon or eBay. However, managing multiple sales channels can quickly become complex without the right tools and integrations.

In this talk, Matthieu De Clercq from The Service Company will present how Odoo can be connected to Shoppingfeed to create a powerful multichannel commerce setup. The session will explain how Odoo acts as the central ERP to manage products, prices, stock and orders, while Shoppingfeed distributes product data to hundreds of marketplaces and marketing channels.

Through a real implementation example, we will demonstrate how this integration simplifies catalog management, synchronizes inventory across channels, and automatically brings marketplace orders back into Odoo. Attendees will gain insights into the architecture of the integration, the business benefits for merchants, and best practices for scaling marketplace operations with Odoo.

This talk is aimed at Odoo partners, integrators, and merchants who want to develop an efficient omnichannel strategy while keeping Odoo as the central source of truth.

(More info : https://shoppingfeed.com/fr/migrer-vers-shoppingfeed)

tracks.description_html:
This session takes a behind-the-scenes look at Odoo Support, explaining how our teams operate and how we deliver assistance to both customers and partners. We will explore what makes Odoo Support different from traditional customer service organizations, considering both the employee perspective and the customer experience.

The presentation will begin with a brief overview of Odoo’s service offering and where Support fits within the broader organization. It will then clarify the distinction between Success Packs and Support, before explaining how the Support team works on a daily basis, including the scale of our global organization and the number of support engineers across Odoo offices. We will also cover the scope of our coverage, available 21.5 hours a day, six days a week, and walk through the different ways users can reach us, including phone, live support, and ticketing. Finally, the session will highlight Odoo’s preventive support approach and how it helps customers avoid issues before they impact their business.

By the end of the session, attendees will have a clear understanding of how Odoo Support is organized, how we collaborate internally, and how we provide a responsive and proactive support experience to our customers and partners worldwide.

tracks.name: Setting Up Odoo for Long-Term Rental: Products, Contracts & Automated recurring Billing
tracks.speaker_line: Tom Sandinha, Odoo Senior Functionnal Consultant at Scalizer
tracks.description_html:
Long-term rental (LTR) is a specific business model that requires precise configuration in Odoo to handle recurring contracts and automated monthly invoicing reliably. Yet many implementations struggle with the same recurring issues: incorrect billing cycles, manual workarounds, and a product setup that doesn't reflect the rental reality.

This session walks through the full functional setup of Odoo for a long-term rental activity, based on a real implementation. Participants will learn how to structure rental products correctly, configure contracts with defined durations and pricing terms, and leverage Odoo's invoicing features to automate recurring monthly billing — without custom development.

Key takeaways include: how to configure products specifically for LTR use cases, which invoicing settings have the biggest impact on billing accuracy, and how to handle common edge cases such as contract renewals, early terminations, and prorated periods.

The value for the audience lies in understanding the full functional chain — not just isolated settings — and walking away with a clear, battle-tested configuration blueprint ready to apply in real projects.

This talk is aimed at Odoo functional consultants, IT managers, and operations teams working in or with companies offering vehicle or equipment rental on long-term contracts.

tracks.name: How to streamline the unavoidable in E-Commerce: fully integrated and highly automated returns processing with Odoo
tracks.speaker_line: Iva Shtembari, Full Stack Consultant at bobco GmbH
tracks.description_html:
Most e-commerce teams think of returns as a warehouse process. A product comes back, a return transfer is validated, and inventory is updated.

But at scale, that is only a small part of the story.

A real return touches customer service, warehouse operations, accounting, payments, eCom, helpdesk, inventory valuation, refund rules, restocking fees, scrapping, and exception handling. If those steps are spread across multiple screens and manual decisions, returns become slow, error-prone, and frustrating for both customers and internal teams.

In this talk, I’ll show how we designed a scalable return workflow in Odoo for high-volume e-commerce operations. The pattern starts with a simple idea: use return categories as the operational decision point. From there, Odoo can decide whether to create a normal return, scrap products immediately, auto-create credit memos, apply restocking fees, trigger Shopify refunds, or route exceptions to the right team.

This talk is about designing the full after-sales loop in Odoo: return intake, warehouse processing, refund accounting, payment execution, and exception management.

What you’ll learn:
- Why returns should be modeled as an end-to-end after-sales workflow, not just a reverse picking.
- How return categories can drive automation across warehouse, accounting, and customer service.
- How to reduce manual return handling without removing operational control.
- How to design credit memo automation safely, including exclusions, restocking fees, and draft/auto-confirm logic.
- How Shopify refund automation can be connected to posted credit memos.
- Where to use activities, Helpdesk tickets, chatter, and operational views for return exceptions.

Each colleague perceives, proposes, and acts — but never without a human "yes" (patented human-in-the-loop governance). Onboarding a new tenant takes minutes, not months, thanks to a patented onboarding flow that provisions a complete Odoo stack automatically.
And it's more than agents: an Enterprise PIM ships in the box, and EU Digital Product Passports (ESPR) are generated automatically from your product data — compliance without extra work. Patent protected.

Odoo partners will leave knowing why an agentic layer is the next migration magnet — and how to position it. Live demo included.

tracks.name: The Global Myth: Why one-size-fits-all doesn’t work in Europe
tracks.speaker_line: Rogier Schoute, Chief Product Officer and Board Member at Mollie at Mollie
tracks.description_html:
The playbook for scaling a technology company sounds simple: build one great product, standardise it, and take it everywhere. Mollie’s journey across Europe tells a different story.

What started as one entrepreneur solving a local payments problem has grown into a European technology company by confronting a fundamental challenge: how do you scale without becoming generic?

Drawing on Mollie’s own growth story, CPO and Board Member Rogier Schoute explores how leaders can decide what to standardise, what needs to stay local, and how to absorb complexity inside the business rather than pass it on to customers. From hyper-localisation across European markets to connecting online and in-person commerce, he shares the product principles behind growing across a fragmented continent while staying close to the people and businesses you serve.

Because in Europe, scale isn’t about making every market the same. It’s about knowing which differences matter.

This session is designed for manufacturers, operations leaders, project managers, and executives responsible for digital transformation.

Drawing on over 400 years of combined manufacturing experience and hundreds of successful Odoo projects, the QOC Innovations team will share the best practices we've seen consistently lead to successful manufacturing implementations. From discovery and process design to production planning, inventory management, change management, and go-live, this session focuses on the decisions that have the biggest impact on long-term success.
You'll learn where manufacturers commonly struggle, how to avoid costly implementation mistakes, and why understanding shop floor operations is just as important as understanding the ERP itself. We'll also share practical lessons from real customer engagements that have helped manufacturers streamline operations, improve visibility, and build a stronger foundation for growth.
Whether you're evaluating Odoo, preparing for an implementation, or looking to optimize an existing system, you'll leave with actionable strategies to reduce project risk, improve adoption, and maximize the value of your ERP investment. This session is designed for manufacturers, operations leaders, project managers, and executives responsible for digital transformation.

tracks.name: From timer to assistant: How Odoo stopped asking you to press start
tracks.speaker_line: Abderraouf Ghrissi from Odoo
tracks.description_html:
For years, the Odoo timesheet meant one thing: remember to hit start on a timer, or rebuild your day from memory on Friday afternoon. We replaced that model with the Timesheet Assistant, a passive layer that watches what you actually worked on and lets you confirm it in one click instead of tracking it in real time. 

This talk walks through how it's built: a local-first companion app that observes windows, browser tabs, and IDE activity on your machine, a rule engine that turns that raw activity into project and task suggestions, and an on-device learning loop that gets better at guessing without any data ever leaving your computer.

tracks.name: Agentic AI-Driven SAP HANA to Odoo Migration at Scale with Zero-Downtime
tracks.speaker_line: Om Prakash Maurya, Delivery Head - CRM & ERP at Ksolves IT USA Inc.
tracks.description_html:
As organizations outgrow the rigidity and rising costs of SAP HANA, Odoo is emerging as the strategic alternative, but migration is rarely straightforward.

This talk reveals how:
- AI intelligently maps SAP HANA data structures, flags field conflicts, and auto-generates assessment reports, dramatically reducing manual analysis effort.
- Agentic AI takes it further by autonomously orchestrating zero-downtime cutovers, continuously scoring migration risk, and escalating issues in real time, compressing go-live timelines to as little as weeks.
- Post-migration agents run autonomously in the background, monitoring data integrity and surfacing reconciliation gaps before they become production incidents, ensuring a smooth transition without requiring constant manual oversight.

Ideal for people and organizations that want to move away from SAP because of escalating costs but remain concerned about losing historical business data, disrupting operations, or undertaking a complex migration.

Key Learnings:
- The hidden cost of staying on SAP HANA, and the ROI case for switching.
- How AI agents compress a months-long migration into weeks without downtime.
- Real pitfalls, honest limitations, and what actually makes a go-live succeed.

tracks.name: "Simplifying the Heavy“ – Odoo for Specialized Rental Workflows
tracks.speaker_line: Tim Freudenthal from HLR Group B.V.
tracks.description_html:
HLR GmbH, a young company based in Hamburg, has been focusing on the rental of highly specialized lifting and hoisting technology such as hydraulic cylinders, chain hoists and slings since 2023. With just 13 employees but in-depth industry expertise, HLR is pursuing ambitious growth plans - supported by a digital infrastructure that needs to be as flexible as its products. In this talk, Tim Freudenthal (HLR GmbH) and Reiner Hannaske (Intero Technologies GmbH) provide practical insights into the introduction of Odoo as a central company platform. They will show how Odoo has become the mainstay of day-to-day business with individually customizable rental periods, complex serial number and warehouse management and the documentation of test certificates.
Special attention is paid to the step-by-step approach: from the requirements workshop to MVP implementation and continuous further development - all with one clear goal: efficient, scalable processes in one system. An inspiring experience report for anyone who wants to master industry-specific complexity with digital ease.

tracks.name: Bankable Business - What the Best Entrepreneurs Do Differently When Dealing with Banks and Investment Funds.
tracks.speaker_line: Solenne Niedercorn-Desouches
tracks.description_html: Profitability alone doesn't make a company investable. In this session, Solenne Niedercorn-Desouches, founder of Finscale and lecturer at HEC Paris, opens the black box of how banks and investment funds actually read a company's file. Drawing on years of conversations with GPs, bankers and CFOs, she walks entrepreneurs through what financiers really look for beyond the numbers: how investor expectations differ from banking logic, which financial structuring choices signal maturity, which metrics actually matter, and why trust and narrative can outweigh a strong balance sheet. A practical, myth-busting session for founders who want to stop pitching blind and start speaking the language their financiers already use.

tracks.name: Automating the Impossible: Heuristic MRP Scheduling for Mid-Sized Companies inside the Odoo Core
tracks.speaker_line: Bernhard Hilfer, ERP Consultant at much. Consulting
tracks.description_html:
In mid-sized manufacturing, successfully processing deep Bills of Materials depends on flawless dependency scheduling. However, manually scheduling thousands of interdependent Work Orders is practically impossible. The inevitable consequences are a cluttered shop floor overflowing with Work-in-Progress (WIP), hidden bottlenecks, and constantly missed delivery dates. While many companies attempt to solve this chaos through costly integrations with external planning tools, this talk will explore a smarter alternative: building lightweight, highly practical scheduling logic directly into the Odoo Enterprise MRP core.

We will demonstrate how leveraging standard priority flags and deadline fields can automatically schedule operations against actual machine capacity. Running these high-volume calculations takes seconds and immediately populates standard Odoo Gantt views with accurate forecasts.

Attendees will walk away with a deep understanding of how to eliminate friction between the sales desk and the factory floor, easily accommodate rush orders, and guarantee verifiable delivery dates - all without ever leaving their primary ERP system.

Key Points of This Talk:

- The operational impact of deep Bills of Materials on manual scheduling workflows
- Why external third-party planning tools often result in expensive data silos
- Architecture overview: embedding custom heuristic MRP logic directly into Odoo
- Aligning material allocation with machine capacity to drastically reduce physical WIP
- Visualizing high-speed capacity calculations within built-in Odoo Gantt views
- Bridging the gap: achieving operational transparency between sales and production

Key Learnings:

- Understand the technical approach to building custom scheduling logic natively in Odoo
- Learn how to utilize standard MO priority flags and deadlines to drive automated sequencing
- Discover actionable strategies to dynamically manage and schedule high-volume rush orders
- Gain the ability to translate complex production data into clear bottleneck forecasts
- Walk away with a blueprint for securing verifiable sales delivery dates based on realistic machine capacity

Target Audience:

- Manufacturing Consultants and Odoo Integrators expanding their MRP capabilities
- Production Managers targeting Mittelstand operations
- Sales Teams requiring realistic, verifiable delivery forecasting

- Migrating data from ongoing, long-lasting projects from legacy software to Odoo

tracks.name: Le doute comme moteur

tracks.description_html: GuiHome est connu pour son parcours dans l’humour. Vidéaste, comédien, humoriste sur scène, chroniqueur chez Quotidien, sociétaire aux Grosses Têtes… il jongle avec toutes ces casquettes depuis des années. Mais derrière l’humoriste se cache aussi un jeune entrepreneur passionné. Producteur de plusieurs humoristes et d’émissions de télévision, organisateur d’un festival d’humour, propriétaire de son restaurant-comedy club… GuiHome n’arrête jamais. Sur le papier, tout ressemble à une belle success story. Mais si tous ces projets n’avaient justement pas vu le jour sans ses angoisses, ses doutes, ses peurs, ses erreurs et son manque de confiance en lui ? Dans ce talk, GuiHome raconte l’envers du décor : comment ce que l’on considère souvent comme des faiblesses peut aussi devenir un moteur pour entreprendre, créer et avancer.

tracks.name: Using Odoo as the Backbone of a Long-Term Strategic Vision
tracks.speaker_line: Olivier Lambert, Directeur Général de Cefora at Squareflow S.A.
tracks.description_html:
Cefora is not a typical organization. As the training and development partner of Belgium’s largest joint committee (CP200), its mission is to help hundreds of thousands of employees continuously develop their skills and remain employable in a rapidly changing economy.

To deliver on that mission at scale, Cefora needed more than an ERP. It needed a platform capable of connecting people, services, processes, and data across an increasingly complex ecosystem.

Together with Odoo and Squareflow, Cefora embarked on a long-term digital transformation journey. What started as a modernization initiative has evolved into the foundation of a sector-wide training ecosystem, supporting everything from course management and learner engagement to operational workflows and service delivery.

Today, Odoo serves as the central platform behind Cefora's mission, integrating a growing network of digital services and enabling the organization to operate more efficiently, respond faster to changing needs, and continuously expand its impact.

And this journey is far from over. With a new CRM platform, expanded service offerings, ambassador lifecycle management, and data-driven decision-making on the roadmap, Cefora is now entering the next phase of its transformation: leveraging Odoo not only as an operational backbone, but as a platform for growth, innovation, and long-term mission activation.

tracks.name: Mastering the Payroll Journal Entry with Swiss Compliance
tracks.speaker_line: Monteiro Da Silva from Sodexis Sàrl
tracks.description_html:
Are you struggling to keep your financial accounting fully aligned with Switzerland's strict, multi-layered payroll regulations? Navigating the complex ledger requirements for Swiss social security (AVS/AI/APG), occupational pensions (LPP), accidents (AANP), and canton-specific withholding taxes (impôt à la source) presents an ongoing compliance and operational challenge for financial and HR teams alike.
Enter the power of a localized ERP solution! Generating a compliant monthly payroll journal entry no longer requires manual cross-referencing, external spreadsheets, or high-risk manual accounting entries. By establishing a robust, automated bridge between HR payroll structures and the general ledger, businesses operating in Switzerland can seamlessly translate complex salary distributions into perfectly balanced, regulation-compliant financial data.
Over the past few years, numerous organizations operating across Switzerland have partnered with Sodexis to continuously improve their Odoo implementation, streamlining operations to ensure smooth, compliant, and scalable financial growth. Sodexis has successfully implemented customized accounting and payroll configurations to enable the seamless tracking, splitting, and posting of localized social deductions directly within the core operational workflow.
Join this session to discover how to achieve complete accounting peace of mind with Swiss payroll compliance—and learn how the collaborative partnership between your operational teams and Sodexis can deliver an efficient, future-proof roadmap for your financial workflows.
Representing the implementation success will be key members of our finance integration team, alongside Noémie (Nemo) Keller, Director of Operations for Sodexis.
Since 2012, Sodexis has been a full-service Odoo Implementation Partner, with a Consulting and Development team focused on maximizing customers’ ROI and user experience. Sodexis is one of the longest-tenured implementation Odoo Partners in the US and has offices also in Switzerland, France, and Austria. Sodexis brings a wealth of experience and valuable expertise to its clients, having successfully implemented over 175 projects and built hundreds of custom applications.
More info: https://sodexis.com/

tracks.name: From Inventory to True WMS: Elevating ODOO with Talk’nPick

tracks.description_html:
Many growing companies reach a point where standard ODOO Inventory is no longer enough to support fast, accurate, and scalable warehouse operations. In this session, we will show how Talkn'Pick transforms ODOO Inventory into a true WMS-level solution — without replacing your ERP.
Talkn'Pick adds process-driven mobile workflows, real-time barcode operations, guided picking, and warehouse floor optimization directly on top of ODOO. Instead of transaction-based screens, users get operationally designed flows that reduce errors, speed up handling, and improve traceability.
We will share practical use cases, performance improvements, and architectural principles that allow companies to scale warehouse efficiency while staying fully inside the ODOO ecosystem.
If you want WMS-level performance without leaving ODOO, this session is for you.

Financial data lived in silos, project tracking was manual and error-prone, and reporting meant spending hours stitching together spreadsheets — leaving management without the real-time visibility they needed to make confident decisions. In partnership with Timus, GKW made the move to Odoo — and the transformation went far beyond a simple software switch. This talk walks you through the full journey: from discovery and migration planning, through the implementation of Accounting and Finance, Project Management, and a powerful reporting layer built on a combination of Odoo's native reporting modules and Power BI dashboards. Attendees will learn how Timus structured the migration to minimise disruption to an active consulting business, how Odoo's unified data model made cross-functional reporting possible for the first time, and how the Power BI integration gave GKW's leadership a live command centre for project profitability, cash flow, and resource utilisation. Key learnings for the audience include: how to approach ERP migration for professional services firms, best practices for combining Odoo's built-in reporting with external BI tools, and how to build dashboards that finance and operations teams actually use. This session is ideal for Odoo partners, implementation consultants, CFOs, and operations leaders in consulting or engineering firms looking to modernise their business management stack without losing months of productivity in the process.

  • Import products with variants and options for Shopify, Wordpress or Prestashop shops
  • Recover blogs from Wordpress and Ghost platforms

tracks.name: The People Layer: The human voyage of Flamant's ERP migration
tracks.speaker_line: Pieter Jan Van Wettere, COO at Odoo
tracks.description_html:
An ERP migration is usually scoped as an IT project.

In practice it is the rare opportunity to look at your organisation honestly: where does it stall, where do you lose time, and which habits survive simply because it has always been that way.

Part one — the road to go-live.

Flamant's migration to Odoo told through the people who had to carry it: the Project Owner connecting business and technology, the Challenger questioning the status quo, the Data Guru making sure no rubbish gets in, and the Key Users who move colleagues from doubt to confidence.

Plus, the choices behind it — a hybrid model of standard Odoo, implementation partner and in-house development, the role AI played, and why a phased rollout beat a big bang.

Part two — where we are now.

The reality on the other side of go-live: which convictions held, which did not, what the organisation actually looks like today, and what we would do differently.

speakers.name: Pieter Jan Van Wettere
speakers.biography_html:
Pieter-Jan Van Wettere holds an MSc in Strategic Marketing from Coventry University, earned while a student job at Colruyt Group was quietly turning into a ten-year retail career.
Those ten years taught him the fundamentals: how a store runs, and how to lead the people running it.
 
From there he moved into retail operations at Lidl, then joined furniture group Beliving as regional sales manager.
He worked his way through buying into category leadership, ending as Category Director for the Exterioo format — nearly ten years of learning how a retail organisation holds together from the stores upward.
 
In 2025 he became COO of Flamant, the Belgian interiors and lifestyle brand, leading the operational organisation across four retail stores, e-commerce, and a wholesale network.
Shortly after, he took on the migration to Odoo — from the business side rather than the IT side, which is exactly what this talk is about.

tracks.name: Stop Building Connectors: A Configuration-Driven Integration Framework for Odoo
tracks.speaker_line: Sebastien Didelot, CEO at akolio
tracks.description_html:
Every Odoo integrator knows the pattern: a new marketplace, a new carrier, a new platform — and yet another bespoke connector to build, test, and maintain. Multiply that across clients and Odoo versions, and integration becomes the single largest source of technical debt and migration pain in an ERP project.

This session presents a different approach: a universal, configuration-driven integration layer, native to Odoo. Instead of one Python module per external system, a multi-protocol API engine (REST, JSON-RPC, SOAP and GraphQL, with Basic / token / OAuth 2.0 authentication), a declarative connector (external system → resources → actions) and a mapping tool let you connect a new source by configuring it — not by launching a development project. When you hit a gap, you extend the framework once and every future integration benefits.

We show this live: connecting a real GraphQL API end-to-end — connection, request body, pagination, and field mapping — in minutes, without writing a new module. Then we share what running this in production teaches you, on a multi-tenant, Kubernetes-hosted Odoo platform where integrations must scale across dozens of instances and survive version upgrades.

Key takeaways: why one-off connectors don't scale and their hidden migration cost; how a config-driven, multi-protocol integration layer works in practice; a no-code example connecting an external API; and production lessons from a multi-tenant Odoo deployment.

Value for the audience: a reusable architectural pattern — not a product — that cuts integration time, lowers long-term maintenance, and stays resilient across Odoo upgrades.

Target audience: Odoo partners, integrators, technical consultants and developers, and functional decision-makers in retail, e-commerce and distribution who manage multiple sales channels and logistics providers.

tracks.name: DirectPaie – The French payslip. Directly in Odoo.
tracks.speaker_line: Fabrice Lucien, Directeur at Yes We Doo
tracks.description_html:
DirectPaie – Et si la paie française devenait enfin un atout dans Odoo ?

Description détaillée
---------------------

La paie française fait peur. Complexe, risquée, chronophage.
Résultat : dans la majorité des projets Odoo, elle reste externalisée, mal intégrée… ou évitée.

Et si c’était une erreur stratégique ?

Dans cette conférence, nous allons challenger cette idée reçue et montrer comment reprendre le contrôle de la paie, sans complexifier vos projets.

Avec DirectPaie, nous avons conçu un moteur de paie pensé dès le départ pour la France et pour Odoo :
- conforme à la réglementation française
- connecté à Odoo
- conçu pour être industrialisable et maintenable dans le temps

Vous verrez concrètement comment intégrer la paie dans votre offre Odoo sans prendre de risque, sans être expert paie, tout en créant une nouvelle source de revenus récurrents.

Nous partagerons également les coulisses du projet :

- comment structurer un moteur de paie fiable (règles, DSN, mises à jour légales)
- et surtout, comment rendre la paie exploitable par des intégrateurs, pas uniquement par des experts paie

L’objectif est simple : faire passer la paie de problème à éviter... à opportunité à saisir !

Points clés à retenir
--------------------

- La paie n’est plus un sujet à contourner dans Odoo
- Il est possible d’être conforme sans être dépendant d’une usine à gaz
- Une architecture moderne permet de sécuriser la paie dans la durée
- Les intégrateurs peuvent reprendre la main sans devenir experts paie
- La paie peut devenir un levier de croissance rentable

Valeur apportée au public
--------------------------

- Une vision claire, concrète et décomplexée de la paie française
- Des clés pour intégrer la paie dans vos projets sans augmenter le risque
- Un nouveau modèle de revenus récurrents à forte valeur
- Une meilleure maîtrise d’un sujet souvent subi

Public cible
------------

- Intégrateurs Odoo (dirigeants, commerciaux, consultants)
- Décideurs (DAF, RAF, dirigeants de PME/ETI)
- Partenaires souhaitant enrichir leur offre avec la paie

tracks.name: Smart Manufacturing in Action: Zerynth’s Odoo Connector
tracks.speaker_line: Fabio Cacciapuoti, Chief Operational Officer at Zerynth
tracks.description_html:
Zerynth’s Odoo Connector empowers manufacturers by seamlessly integrating IoT and AI with both modern and legacy industrial machinery. This integration enables real-time production optimization, cost and energy consumption reduction, and supports a sustainable Industry 5.0 transformation.

In this session, we will present a compelling customer success story from a manufacturing company that digitalized traditionally hard-to-integrate production assets. By using the Zerynth Connector, the company was able to extract valuable data—such as production performance, energy usage, and anomalous machine behavior—and integrate it directly into Odoo. This not only streamlined data collection and automated the Odoo production module but also enhanced operational efficiency and promoted energy savings.

The Zerynth Connector allows for fast, non-invasive connectivity to industrial equipment, accelerating the digital transformation of shop floors. Additionally, it features Smart Report, an AI-powered tool that simplifies the creation of detailed sustainability reports and supports ESG certification efforts. This functionality helps manufacturers meet regulatory requirements while strengthening their commitment to environmental responsibility.

tracks.name: Autonomous Unit Test Generation with an AI Agent Loop: From Untested Code to Reliable Odoo Modules at Scale
tracks.speaker_line: Sebastian Kühnel Bozzo, Developer at twio.tech AG
tracks.description_html:
Maintaining reliable unit tests across customized Odoo modules is one of the most time-consuming and neglected parts of development, especially when working across multiple clients, each with their own business logic and edge cases. The result is often fragile codebases, hidden regressions, and costly debugging cycles in production. In this talk, we present a practical approach to tackling this problem using an AI agent loop that assists developers in generating, validating, and refining unit tests directly from real module code. Rather than relying on one-shot AI prompts, we introduce a structured loop that analyzes the module, proposes test coverage, executes tests, and iteratively improves them based on execution feedback until they become more reliable, meaningful, and executable.

In this talk, we will look at:
- How the AI agent loop works in practice
- Why naive AI-generated tests fail in real Odoo environments, and how iterative execution loops solve this problem
- The role of human-in-the-loop validation to ensure the generated tests actually cover meaningful business logic and real-world edge cases
- Common failure cases we encountered, including tests that pass without testing real logic, missing Odoo context and data dependencies, and tests exposing real bugs in production code
- How to integrate this approach into a real development workflow without disrupting existing practices

Key Learnings:
- How to design an AI agent loop that goes beyond simple prompt-based test generation and produces executable, meaningful tests
- Why execution feedback is critical to avoid false positives and useless test coverage
- How to detect and fix common issues in AI-generated tests, including missing context, weak assertions, and misleading “green” tests
- Why human validation remains critical when generating tests for complex business logic and custom Odoo implementations

Intended Target Audience:
- Odoo developers, technical leads, and consultants who work with custom modules and want to improve code reliability without dramatically increasing development overhead.

It is particularly relevant to:
- Developers working on custom Odoo implementations where test coverage is limited or inconsistent
- Technical leads looking for scalable ways to standardize testing across multiple clients
- Teams interested in applying AI not as a gimmick, but as a structured tool integrated into real development workflows

tracks.name: dooLex - Transforming Odoo into a legal practice system
tracks.speaker_line: Suzanne Mulier, Change & Project Manager at Cloudware NV
tracks.description_html:
Law firms, notaries and bailiffs run on deadlines, confidentiality and billable time; yet most still juggle separate tools for intake, case management, time tracking and accounting. This session shows how we turned standard Odoo into dooLex, a fully integrated practice-management system (PMS) built specifically for legal professionals in Belgium.

We'll show how the core of a legal practice; from the first client intake all the way through to billing and accounting; comes together in one connected environment, with Odoo acting as the central PMS and integrating with a dedicated high-end document-management system (DMS) such as NetDocuments or iManage. Expect a live look at the platform in action and a sense of how Odoo's building blocks can be shaped to fit a regulated, document-heavy profession.

Attendees will walk away with the criteria for solid verticalization - how to recognise which opportunities are worth turning into genuine excellence and expertise - along with the design choices that mattered most and the lessons we took from crafting dooLex.

tracks.name: Integration Ardis & Odoo
tracks.speaker_line: Carolien Van Eyck, Project manager at Dynapps
tracks.description_html: Norm is a Belgian manufacturer of custom kitchen and bathroom furniture that implemented Odoo as its central ERP, with a bidirectional integration with Ardis — their CNC cutting optimization software — as a hard requirement for go-live. From Odoo, confirmed manufacturing orders are written to a SQL database on Norm's internal network, where Ardis picks them up, groups them into production batches, and optimizes the cutting plans. Ardis then feeds back production status updates, actual plate consumption, and pallet numbers after packing to Odoo via an API. The main technical challenges were unit conversion from mm² to m², barcode matching (Ardis uses a "W" prefix that had to be stripped), decoupling the production batch number from the MO status update, and the decision to exclude remainder plates from automatic stock deduction. Norm went live on 24 November 2025, seven months after kick-off, with a smooth go-live.

tracks.name: When Your Odoo Database Explodes: Understanding PG TOAST and How We Reduced 500GB to 60GB
tracks.speaker_line: Cristhian Ampudia, Asistente de Infraestructura at TRESCLOUD
tracks.description_html:
As Odoo databases grow, hidden inefficiencies can silently increase storage usage and severely impact performance. One of the most overlooked causes is PostgreSQL TOAST (The Oversized-Attribute Storage Technique), especially when large binary data—such as base64-encoded images—is improperly stored in database fields.

In this talk, we present a real-world case where a client's Odoo database grew to over 500GB due to excessive storage of base64 images inside PostgreSQL tables. This led to performance degradation, slow backups, and increased infrastructure costs.

We will explain how TOAST works in PostgreSQL, how it affects Odoo installations, and how to identify when your database is suffering from TOAST-related bloat. We will also walk through the diagnostic process, including SQL queries and tools used to analyze table size, TOAST usage, and data patterns.

Most importantly, we will demonstrate the solution that reduced the database size from 500GB to 60GB, including data cleanup strategies, architectural improvements, and best practices to prevent this issue in future implementations.

Attendees will leave with practical techniques to audit their own databases, optimize storage, and significantly improve Odoo performance.

This session is ideal for Odoo developers, DevOps engineers, and technical consultants managing large-scale Odoo deployments.

tracks.name: Escaping the Inventory Freeze: Just-in-Time Procurement in Odoo Enterprise
tracks.speaker_line: Tânia Manco, ERP Consultant at much. Consulting
tracks.description_html:
Why does stock sit dead on warehouse shelves? In standard Odoo, procurement counts forward. When a customer places an order for a future date, the system looks at the vendor lead time and triggers a purchase order immediately. If a supplier takes five days to deliver an item needed in a month, Odoo buys it now. The goods arrive weeks too early, locking up cash and taking up warehouse space. Meanwhile, standard reservation rules block that stock, preventing other active orders from using it.

To prevent such an inventory freeze, especially for high-volume warehouses, we built a backward-scheduling engine for Odoo Enterprise.

Instead of counting forward from the purchase date, the engine starts at the customer’s requested delivery date and counts backward. It determines the exact day to place the purchase order and the precise window to reserve warehouse stock. To match real-world supply chains, the calculation uses only weekdays (Monday to Friday).

The engine also isolates buying requirements for special project agreements from routine warehouse restocking, ensuring contract pricing applies correctly. When vendor lead times change, Odoo automatically updates open purchase orders and internal warehouse transfers. This automation keeps stock moving, frees up working capital, and cuts out manual scheduling work for procurement teams.

Key Points of This Talk:

- Optimising Odoo standard stock reservations with an automatically calculated backward-scheduled reservation window.
- Calculating purchasing deadlines backward from the sales delivery date using only weekdays.
- Separating specific project agreement purchases from standard restocking to maintain correct pricing.
- Automatically recalculating warehouse transfers and open orders when vendor lead times change.

Key Learnings:

- How to use Just-In-Time reservation windows to keep inventory available longer and free up capital.
- How to set up backward scheduling to tell your purchasing team exactly when to order based on customer requests.
- How to keep project-specific supply chains separate to protect special vendor pricing.
- How to handle vendor delays by having the system automatically adjust warehouse schedules.

Target Audience:

- Warehouse Managers and Operations Directors handling complex supply chains in Odoo
- Procurement Specialists managing complex vendor agreements
- Odoo Consultants and Architects looking for maintainable customization strategies

tracks.name: Circular Economy: How to Run a Refurbishment Business in Odoo
tracks.speaker_line: Jean-Elie Sonnet from Odoo
tracks.description_html:
The circular economy is no longer just a trend—it is a business necessity and a massive global market. 

In this session, we will introduce you to the new "electronics refurbishment" industry solution: a turnkey, pre-configured framework designed to run your entire refurbishment business inside Odoo. Along with out-of-the-box configurations, this industry package includes a brand-new module called "Product Conversion & Grading Management." We will show you how this module allows you to easily convert a product from one quality grading to another directly within a Manufacturing Order.

We will run through a full end-to-end loop live on stage:

  • Bulk Purchase: Buying unconditioned raw inventory.
  • Identification: Assigning unique serialization and intake grading.
  • Repair Pipeline: Sending the unit to the workshop.
  • Component Consumption: Tracking replacement parts used during repair.
  • Restocking: Automatically moving finalized, graded stock back to inventory.
  • Web Sales & Invoicing: Selling via the Odoo eCommerce website and generating the invoice.
  • Reporting: Pulling real-time margin and profitability reports.
Finally, we will solve the ultimate compliance headache by demystifying the VAT margin scheme. You will discover the exact accounting workflow that automatically isolates the real purchase cost of unique items, allowing you to seamlessly regularize margin taxes.

The goal of this talk is simple: To show you an incredibly easy, standard way to build a highly profitable circular refurbishing company using Odoo.

tracks.name: Multi-Agent Swarms for High-Performance ERP Migration in Odoo
tracks.speaker_line: Serena Palazzo, AI Team Leader at Rapsodoo
tracks.description_html:
Enterprise ERP migrations toward Odoo are increasingly constrained by transformation complexity, heterogeneous schemas, and the need for near-zero downtime execution.

In this talk, we introduce a multi-agent swarm architecture designed to accelerate and parallelize data migration workflows through autonomous specialization and distributed decision-making. The system decomposes migration tasks into atomic responsibilities handled by coordinated AI agents, including schema decomposition agents, mapping inference agents, validation swarms, and conflict resolution agents.

We present a coordination layer inspired by swarm intelligence principles, where agents dynamically negotiate transformation strategies based on confidence scoring, constraint satisfaction signals, and historical migration performance metrics. This enables parallel exploration of multiple migration strategies while converging on optimal transformation paths.

The framework—internally referred to as the “AI Migration Syndicate”—is implemented on top of cloud-native execution environments with event-driven orchestration, allowing scalable execution of migration tasks across distributed workers. Special focus is given to deterministic fallback mechanisms, auditability, and reconciliation guarantees required in enterprise ERP contexts.

We conclude with real-world benchmarks demonstrating significant improvements in migration throughput, reduced manual intervention, and improved consistency in large-scale migrations into Odoo.

In high-volume dropshipping, a bloated IT infrastructure is the silent killer of scaling - and margins.

Managing hundreds of thousands of products across a fragmented software landscape disrupts vendor relationships and leaves businesses unable to react to rapid market price shifts.

This talk explores how we resolved this issue by consolidating operations, transforming Odoo 19 Enterprise into a "One-Stop" hub that harmonizes a large Shopware frontend with a lean, automated backend.

We will walk you through the journey of building a robust, step-based synchronization framework capable of handling extreme variant complexity - exceeding 400 options per product - while enabling real-time dropshipping automation.

From centralizing the product master to executing bulk vendor price updates across a quarter-million SKUs, this talk demonstrates how to scale a large catalog.

Key Points of this Talk:

- Infrastructure challenges of managing 250,000 dropshipping SKUs
- Overcoming the variant bottleneck: functional setup for products with 400+ options
- Designing a step-based synchronization framework between Shopware and Odoo 19
- Automating backend procurement triggers directly from frontend retail sales
- Centralizing vendor data to execute rapid bulk price updates
- Technical choices for balancing extreme data volumes with long-term Odoo stability

Key Learnings:

- How to replace fragmented legacy IT software landscapes with a single Odoo Enterprise core
- Methods to transition the operational "Source of Truth" in complex, multi-variant retail environments
- Strategies to architect automated dropshipping pipelines that eliminate manual intervention
- How to manage large-scale vendor data updates without causing database performance drops
- Project insights on balancing immediate business logic requirements with ERP maintainability

Target Audience:

- CEOs, COOs, and Operations Managers in Wholesale or Dropshipping
- Odoo Functional Consultants and Solution Architects
- IT Directors managing multi-system e-commerce environments

tracks.name: The Two Hats of Odoo Python: Powering Core Logic vs. Driving User Experience
tracks.speaker_line: Gary Dolorfino, Engineering Expert at much. Consulting
tracks.description_html:
This talk differentiates "Client-Facing Python" (UI events, dynamic views, computed fields) from "Core Backend Python" (business rules, data integrity, scheduled tasks, wizards) in Odoo development. Understanding this separation is crucial for building responsive, maintainable, and robust applications. The session will provide a framework for structuring Python code, optimizing performance and being intentional about UX implementation.

Key Points:

- Defining "Client-Facing" Python: onchange methods, button actions, dynamic UI Python (e.g., domains, field attributes), and UI-reflected computed fields.
- Defining "Core Backend" Python: ORM overrides (create(), write(), unlink()), scheduled actions, server actions, and complex wizard/data processing logic.
- Interaction & Data Flow: Examining how client-facing Python often acts as a gateway or pre/post-processor for core backend logic, and the pivotal role of the ORM as the bridge.
- Architectural Patterns & Best Practices: Strategies for keeping client-facing Python lean and responsive, isolating heavy logic in core backend Python (including considerations for asynchronous processing where applicable), ensuring security through input validation, and enhancing the testability of both code types.
- Practical Case Studies: Illustrating concepts with real-world examples, such as refactoring a performance-degrading onchange method and designing a button action that orchestrates multiple backend operations efficiently.
- Optimizing for Responsiveness: Actionable techniques to ensure client-facing Python supports, rather than hinders, a fluid and fast user interface.

Key Learnings:

- Attendees will be able to architect Odoo modules by clearly distinguishing the roles of their server-side Python code, separating UI-centric logic from core business operations.
- Attendees will learn to implement strategies to optimize Python code for responsive user interfaces, identifying and mitigating common performance bottlenecks associated with client-facing scripts.
- Attendees will understand how to design robust and efficient interactions and data flows between client-facing and core backend Python layers.
- Attendees will take away best practices for security (especially input validation from UI interactions) and testability tailored to the distinct characteristics of each type of Python code.
- Attendees will be equipped to refactor existing Odoo customizations for improved performance, maintainability, and scalability by applying these architectural principles.

Target Audience:
- Odoo Python Developers (Beginner and Intermediate)
- Odoo Technical Architects
- Technical Consultants involved in designing and implementing Odoo customizations
- Software Engineers working with the Odoo framework

tracks.name: Custom Manufacturing: Driving Performance with Odoo
tracks.speaker_line: Mélanie Delfosse from Metrum
tracks.description_html:
Manufacturers producing highly customized products face unique operational challenges. Every order can introduce new specifications, production constraints and planning complexities, making standard manufacturing processes difficult to apply.

In this live demonstration, we will showcase how Odoo can become the operational backbone of a custom manufacturing company. From quotation to delivery, attendees will discover how standard Odoo, targeted custom developments and AI-powered capabilities work together to streamline operations while preserving the flexibility required for engineer-to-order and make-to-order businesses.

The session will cover the complete manufacturing lifecycle, including:

Configuring complex products and capturing customer requirements
Engineering and production preparation
Procurement and material availability
Production planning and shop floor execution
Inventory and traceability
Quality management
Real-time operational monitoring and decision support

Beyond demonstrating features, we will explain the functional decisions behind a successful implementation: when to rely on standard Odoo, where customization creates real business value, and how AI can automate repetitive tasks, support decision-making and improve operational performance.

Attendees will leave with practical implementation patterns and actionable insights to build scalable, high-performance manufacturing operations while maintaining the flexibility that custom production demands.

tracks.name: Transforming LPG Cylinder Lifecycle Management with Odoo at Puma Energy
tracks.speaker_line: Chintan Shah, CEO, Brainvire at Brainvire
tracks.description_html:
Managing LPG cylinders at scale is not just an inventory challenge. It is a moving lifecycle of filled, empty, damaged, returned, and refilled cylinders passing through plants, warehouses, dealers, customers, and intercompany networks. For Puma Energy, limited visibility across these movements created risk around cylinder losses, deposit tracking, return accuracy, and logistics control.

In this session, Brainvire cuts through that complexity. We will show how Odoo was used to bring the entire LPG cylinder lifecycle into one connected operating system across Inventory, Sales, Purchase, and Accounting. With lot and serial number tracking, every cylinder became uniquely traceable from dispatch to refill to return.

We will dive into custom workflows for refill, dispatch, return, intercompany transfers, virtual locations, barcode tracking, and RFID visibility.

The result is complete lifecycle control, reduced losses, faster logistics execution, and accurate financial tracking of cylinder deposits through one scalable Odoo foundation.

tracks.name: Stop Answering the Same Tickets: Building a Self-Teaching Helpdesk with AI in Odoo 19
tracks.speaker_line: Mike Schulz, Senior Expert ERP Consulting at much. Consulting
tracks.description_html:
Service companies lose thousands of hours when their support teams are trapped answering the same Level-1 questions every single day. Without an automated system to record and share answers, agents constantly retype known solutions, which causes massive ticket backlogs and outdated knowledge bases.

To fix this structural bottleneck, we built a low-code, self-teaching loop completely inside the Odoo Enterprise v19 user interface.

We put a pipeline together by configuring three distinct native AI agents, linked with simple Automated Actions and basic Python UI snippets: an “initial responder” utilizing RAG, to answer clients using approved data, an “auditor” to check how tickets were closed, and a “writer” drafting new Knowledge Base articles By plugging in your own OpenAI or Gemini key directly into the frontend, this setup completely skips the need to build or maintain complex custom code modules. This working model proves that businesses can automatically turn daily ticket answers into permanent company documentation, cutting down future support volume and making advanced AI setups a practical reality.

Key Points of this Talk:

- Automating the Hand-Off: Configure Odoo Enterprise Helpdesk to trigger native ai.agents via Automated Actions.
- Forcing Factual Answers: Deploy native RAG parameters to restrict AI responses to approved Knowledge Base data.
- Skipping Custom Code: Evaluate how agents solved tickets using basic frontend Python snippets without custom module development.
- Self-Writing Documentation: Chain AI agents to automatically draft Odoo v19 Knowledge articles from closed tickets.
- Staying in the UI: Build this entire self-improving AI loop without ever leaving the native Odoo frontend.

Key Learnings:

- How to turn complex AI concepts into accessible, low-code Odoo v19 workflows.
- How to launch native AI agents using Automated Actions and simple screen logic.
- How to automatically turn human-resolved tickets into standard Knowledge Base articles.
- How to build a self-improving support system without heavy developer resources.
- How to set strict RAG boundaries to maintain data accuracy and prevent hallucinations.

Target Audience:

Business Leaders, Executives, and Functional Consultants using Odoo Enterprise v19+

This presentation demonstrates how an integrated Odoo platform enables a newly established crafts business to digitalise its operations, grow efficiently and scale successfully.

tracks.name: Odoo goes offline
tracks.speaker_line: Antoine Rousseau from Odoo
tracks.description_html:
Picture a typical day at the office: Sales teams are sending quotations, consultants are logging timesheets, accountants are validating invoices... everything is running smoothly.

Then, without warning, the lights go out. The internet is gone. A complete power outage brings the entire office to a halt.

Or does it?
Not if you're running Odoo.

Join us for a live demonstration of Offline Mode in Odoo 20 and discover how Odoo keeps your business moving, even without an internet connection.

During this session, you'll learn:

  • The prerequisites for working offline

  • How the interface adapts with a dedicated offline UI

  • How to browse, search, create, and edit records offline

  • How to archive and unarchive records

  • How to delete records

  • How synchronization works, including the queue and the tools available to monitor and manage it

Because business doesn't stop when the connection does.

tracks.name: The Last Unfakeable Thing - What our failed virtual exhibition taught us about digitising the wrong half of the business
tracks.speaker_line: Denis Delforge, CEO at Brussels Expo
tracks.description_html:
In 2020, with 120,000 m² of exhibition halls standing empty, we decided to build our own virtual trade show platform. It crashed. Meanwhile, other platforms raised extraordinary valuations on the same premise and then the bubble deflated just as fast.

Five years on, physical gathering is thriving. Denis Delforge, CEO of Brussels Expo, argues the entire industry made the same mistake: we tried to digitise the experience, when what needed digitising was the relationship. Who actually comes through the door, why, and what happens next, a question venues have never been able to answer.

An honest account of a failure, a bubble, and what a 1935 building is doing about it now: white-label ticketing, on-site data, and why the most analogue business in the world is becoming a data business.

tracks.name: Streamlining Sustainability: A Step-by-Step Guide to Odoo's ESG Configuration and Environmental Reporting
tracks.speaker_line: Anas Ouasmi, Business Analyst at Sodexis
tracks.description_html:
As regulatory bodies worldwide tighten disclosure requirements, Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) reporting has shifted from a corporate social responsibility checkbox to a critical compliance necessity. However, aggregating fragmented data from supply chains, energy bills, manufacturing outputs, and corporate travel often leaves sustainability officers buried under manual spreadsheets. How can businesses establish a single source of truth for their sustainability metrics without adding immense administrative overhead?
This session offers a comprehensive guide to navigating Odoo's newly enhanced sustainability architecture. We will explore how to model your company's environmental footprint directly within your ERP ecosystem. By connecting Odoo's core modules such as Purchase, Fleet, Manufacturing, and Accounting with native carbon accounting engines, organizations can capture resource consumption metrics automatically at the point of transaction.
Attendees will learn how to configure emission factors, map energy consumption metrics (Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions), and establish tracking parameters for waste management and sustainable sourcing. We will also address how to customize data input criteria using Odoo Studio to meet specific local or international frameworks (such as CSRD or GRI), optimize calculation templates, and build dynamic sustainability dashboards. This ensures management teams have real-time visibility into their carbon intensity and green targets.
Join this practical session to transform compliance data tracking from a reactive annual burden into a proactive, automated workflow built entirely inside Odoo.

tracks.name: How a €30M+ Supplement Manufacturer Is Moving from Legacy Tools to Odoo
tracks.speaker_line: Ferry Kluger, Founder at bobco GmbH
tracks.description_html:
TISSO is a German nutritional supplement company founded in 1999. More than 20 years later, the company has grown into a €30M+ business with 159 employees and a complex operating model across own-brand B2C sales, subscriptions, B2B therapist and export business, and contract manufacturing.

From the outside, this looks like a modern supplement brand and manufacturer. Behind the scenes, the operational reality was more fragmented: Magento for eCommerce, bespoke ERP as a legacy order backbone, DATEV for accounting execution, Wrike and Google Sheets for coordination, and many manual handoffs between teams.

TISSO did not need “another tool.” It needed a real operating backbone.

In this session, TISSO and bob will share how the company approached Odoo as a phased business transformation: first stabilizing the commercial and finance backbone, then expanding toward Shopify, therapist portal improvements, procurement, inventory, and production.

The key decision was not to force a risky big-bang transformation. Instead, the first live scope focused on the narrowest slice that could create measurable business value: Order-to-Cash, subscriptions, therapist logic, fulfillment execution, invoicing, accounting operations, and reconciliation. This allowed the team to deprecate major legacy anchors while avoiding unnecessary go-live risk around full inventory, production, and valuation.

The long-term vision is broader: Odoo as the central system connecting multi-channel sales, finance, procurement, inventory, and production. But the implementation strategy was deliberately disciplined: prove the backbone first, simplify where possible, challenge unnecessary customizations, and only expand once the business has a stable operational baseline.

This talk is for companies and Odoo partners dealing with real mid-market complexity: legacy systems, partial previous implementations, custom code, multiple revenue streams, manufacturing requirements, finance dependencies, and teams that still rely heavily on spreadsheets and key-person knowledge.

What you’ll learn:

- How to scope an Odoo transformation for a mature company without creating big-bang go-live risk.
- Why the first ERP phase should focus on operational backbone, not maximum system replacement.
- How to decide what belongs in V1 and what must be delayed, even when the long-term ambition is much bigger.
- How TISSO approached Order-to-Cash, subscriptions, therapist business logic, fulfillment, finance handoffs, and reconciliation in Odoo.
- Why inventory, production, and procurement often need to be phased carefully rather than forced into the first go-live.
- How to use Odoo as the foundation for future transformation: Shopify migration, Odoo 19 upgrade, therapist portal expansion, inventory rollout, procurement, and production light.
- How customer and partner teams can work together during discovery, scope design, cutover, go-live, and hypercare.
- What other growing manufacturers can learn from TISSO’s journey from fragmented tools to one operating backbone.

tracks.name: Scaling Support Excellence: Managing 100+ Daily Tickets Across Multiple Helpdesk Teams at GCU with Odoo
tracks.speaker_line: Anas Ouasmi, Business Analyst at Sodexis
tracks.description_html:
Are you struggling to keep up with an ever-increasing volume of customer support requests? Do tickets get lost in transit, or delayed due to manual routing inefficiencies across different internal departments? Managing multi-tier or departmental service desks presents a classic operational challenge: maintaining rapid response times without compromising service quality.
Enter GCU's modern support infrastructure! By leveraging Odoo Helpdesk, GCU transformed its support ecosystem to efficiently handle a heavy load of more than 100 tickets daily. This digital transformation replaced disjointed communication channels with a single, cohesive ticketing framework tailored for diverse operational and technical helpdesk teams.
With an intelligent automation layer, incoming inquiries are dynamically classified and assigned to specialized teams according to expertise, priority, and SLA metrics. Over the past year, this system has allowed GCU to process thousands of incoming issues, dramatically reducing resolution times and boosting user satisfaction across the organization. Service managers now gain real-time visibility through comprehensive analytical dashboards that track team performance and ticket bottlenecks.
Join this session to discover how GCU mapped its complex multi-team workflows to Odoo's native architecture, engineered robust automated workflows, and successfully scaled its operations to ensure a smooth, sustainable support journey.

tracks.name: One Distillery's Problem Becomes an Industry's Platform
tracks.speaker_line: Sebastian Navarro, Growth Lead & Technical Associate at MasterDistiller
tracks.description_html:
MasterDistiller began with a single distillery and a problem the market could not solve. When a young whisky distillery set out to grow, it faced the same two options as everyone else: a sea of disconnected spreadsheets and paper records, or bulky generic ERP software that did not understand a distillery business. This talk tells the story of what came next, how the answer came from an industry-specific system built on the Odoo platform, and where it is heading.

Whisky demands full traceability, accurate maturation costing, and a single source of truth connecting production to finance, sales and planning across decades. The MasterDistiller team will show how Odoo's breadth becomes the foundation for a solution this specific, and why a vertical built on an open platform serves the spirits industry better than any of the old alternatives. MasterDistiller now supports distilleries across the UK, US, Canada and Australia, and every feature built for one client becomes a capability all of them can use.

Looking towards the future, because the platform is open source, extendible and easy to connect into, MasterDistiller is continually developing, including plugging emerging technologies like AI into the system to solve real business problems. The team will share the framework behind this, what the company calls Intelligent Distilling, as the next step in its journey.

Attendees will leave with a clear, practical view of how Odoo partners use platform breadth combined with industry depth to generate real value for their clients.

tracks.name: From CAD to ERP: Creating a Single Source of Truth with SolidWorks, Onshape and Odoo
tracks.speaker_line: Eduardo Magdalena García, Founder & CEO at C2i Change 2 improve Optimización de procesos, S.L.
tracks.description_html:
When information does not flow, companies lose time, money and competitiveness.
In many manufacturing companies, engineering teams create products, assemblies, bills of materials and technical documentation in CAD systems such as SolidWorks or Onshape. However, much of this information never reaches the ERP because manually transferring and maintaining it is too time-consuming and error-prone.
As designs evolve, data quickly becomes outdated, duplicated or inconsistent across departments. As a result, many companies are unable to fully leverage the capabilities of Odoo Manufacturing, Inventory, Purchasing, Projects and other business applications because critical product information is either incomplete or disconnected from the engineering source.
This session explores how a Single Source of Truth approach can bridge the gap between engineering and business operations. Based on real-world CAD-ERP integration projects currently used in manufacturing environments, attendees will discover how SolidWorks, Onshape and Odoo can work together to create a connected digital workflow where product data, bills of materials, design changes, documentation and images remain synchronized throughout the entire product lifecycle.
A live demonstration based on real customer implementations will show how engineering information can flow automatically from CAD into Odoo, reducing manual work, improving traceability and enabling more reliable decision-making across engineering, purchasing, manufacturing and inventory teams.
Attendees will learn:
• Why critical engineering information often never reaches the ERP.
• How disconnected systems create inefficiencies, errors and hidden costs.
• How a Single Source of Truth approach improves consistency, collaboration and traceability.
• How SolidWorks, Onshape and Odoo can work together in real manufacturing environments.
This session is intended for manufacturing companies, engineering teams, operations managers, Odoo partners and anyone interested in improving industrial processes through better information management and system integration.

tracks.name: From 5 tools to 1 platform: how our client in the energy market runs its entire solar installation business in Odoo, from lead to EcoCare subscription
tracks.speaker_line: Jochem Bauwmans and Cindy Singh, Project manager at Dynapps
tracks.description_html: Our client installs solar panels, batteries, heat pumps and charging stations for B2C and B2B customers across Belgium. Before Odoo they ran on Teamleader for CRM, Simple-Simon for technician scheduling, AppSheet for on-site checklists, Google Drive for the customer file, SolarEdge for design and monitoring, and ClearFacts for accounting —  five disconnected tools with constant copy-paste between them and no single view of a deal, a job or a customer. In this session we show how Dynapps consolidated that entire stack into one Odoo platform covering the full lifecycle: lead capture across web/portal/socials, a three-pipeline CRM (B2B, particulier, EcoCare), commissioning models per salesperson, quote duplication and PDF templating, automated Google Drive folder creation per opportunity, a SolarEdge Designer deep-link directly on the lead, mobile-friendly site-visit and installation checklists with sketches, photos and conditional fields, employee scheduling and work-order e-signature for the field technician, inspection registration and single-line-diagram handover, helpdesk with SLAs and multiple teams, tickets auto-created from SolarEdge alerts, recurring EcoCare maintenance subscriptions with SEPA direct debit, and an accountant-friendly handover to ACS. We share how a service installer with 35 internal users runs the whole company end-to-end without leaving Odoo for its day-to-day core business processes.

tracks.name: Odoo Tours: The easy way to test workflows and onboard users
tracks.speaker_line: Jens Boons from Odoo
tracks.description_html:
As an Odoo functional consultant or project manager, you know the pain: you spend hours configuring the perfect workflow, only for a minor configuration change or an app update to quietly disrupt it. Testing everything manually before go-live is a massive time sink. What if you could build a dynamic system that handles both user onboarding and automated business flow testing—without writing a single line of code?

Enter Odoo Tours.

In this presentation, we will explore the immense functional power of the Tour framework. We'll show you how to map out your real-world business use cases into interactive walkthroughs that train your users, and how to instantly repurpose those exact same walkthroughs to validate your configurations. If you want to automate your day-to-day testing, reduce manual QA effort, and guarantee smooth user adoption, this session is for you.

What we will cover:

  • The Functional Blueprint of a Tour: What is an Odoo tour from a business perspective, and how does it map to your standard operational workflows?

  • Onboarding vs. Quality Assurance: How the exact same tool can actively guide a new salesperson through a CRM pipeline, or run automated in the background to verify a multi-step delivery process.

  • Mastering the Tour Recorder: A completely non-technical, step-by-step look at using Odoo’s built-in visual recorder to map clicks, inputs, and button presses simply by clicking through the system.

  • Live Fail Demo: We will visually record a standard business flow and execute it. Then, we will make a realistic functional configuration change (like making a field required or hiding a button) to show exactly how the tour catches the failure and flags the broken workflow.

tracks.description_html:
Mastering demand forecasting and production planning is a heavy process for any manufacturing business, but Odoo's Master Production Schedule (MPS) is here to secure your path. In this session, we will break down core MPS concepts and demonstrate exactly how to operate the tool. Beyond the basics, we will dive into implementation best practices and highlight the critical pitfalls to avoid, ensuring your supply chain remains robust, automated, and free from costly bottlenecks.

The highlight of this talk centers on the exciting new UX features built to completely transform your planning workflow. Discover how a modernized, intuitive dashboard removes the friction from complex data entry, while powerful new tools allow you to automatically populate forecasts and manage batch sizes with just a few clicks. Whether you are looking to optimize your raw materials or simply want to see the latest front-end enhancements in action, this talk will give you the blueprint to elevate your production planning strategy.
