tracks.name: Consolidating the Stack: Replacing WooCommerce with Native Odoo Enterprise eCommerce Extensions
tracks.speaker_line: Tomás Van Loock, ERP Consultant at much. Consulting
tracks.description_html:
B2B2B hardware resellers frequently suffer from fragmented digital architectures, forcing them to maintain complex integrations between external platforms like WooCommerce and their core ERP system. For Cisco Meraki distributor Cloud Controlled, this ecosystem disconnect resulted in constant manual data synchronization, isolated product specifications, and a critical inability to track mandatory end-user data during the standard checkout process.

By migrating the entire operation to the Odoo Enterprise eCommerce and Website apps, we eliminated the WooCommerce middleware entirely and built directly on top of the native ERP data structure. We extended the core Odoo architecture to enable nested category inheritance for deep technical specifications, implemented dynamic real-time fetching of customer lead times directly from standard inventory models, and built a customized B2B2B checkout flow that captures required end-user delivery addresses for reseller compliance automatically.

This single Odoo environment permanently removed the need to sync separate platforms or update web catalogs by hand. Automatically pushing technical data to the storefront cut out hours of weekly admin work on lead times. It also reduced routine technical inquiries, meaning the sales team spent significantly less time answering basic hardware questions.

Key Points of this Talk:

- Removing WooCommerce: Replacing external web shop middleware with native Odoo Enterprise eCommerce apps.
- Smart Product Categories: Extending Odoo's category model so subcategories automatically inherit technical data.
- Live Lead Times: Automatically pulling real-time customer lead times from inventory straight to the website frontend.
- Strict B2B2B Checkout: Changing the regular Odoo eCommerce checkout flow to enforce mandatory end-user address tracking.
- Automatic Data Flow: Letting product specifications automatically pass through complex nested subcategories.

Key Learnings:

tracks.description_text:
B2B2B hardware resellers frequently suffer from fragmented digital architectures, forcing them to maintain complex integrations between external platforms like WooCommerce and their core ERP system. For Cisco Meraki distributor Cloud Controlled, this ecosystem disconnect resulted in constant manual data synchronization, isolated product specifications, and a critical inability to track mandatory end-user data during the standard checkout process.
By migrating the entire operation to the Odoo Enterprise eCommerce and Website apps, we eliminated the WooCommerce middleware entirely and built directly on top of the native ERP data structure. We extended the core Odoo architecture to enable nested category inheritance for deep technical specifications, implemented dynamic real-time fetching of customer lead times directly from standard inventory models, and built a customized B2B2B checkout flow that captures required end-user delivery addresses for reseller compliance automatically.
This single Odoo environment permanently removed the need to sync separate platforms or update web catalogs by hand. Automatically pushing technical data to the storefront cut out hours of weekly admin work on lead times. It also reduced routine technical inquiries, meaning the sales team spent significantly less time answering basic hardware questions.
Key Points of this Talk:
- Removing WooCommerce: Replacing external web shop middleware with native Odoo Enterprise eCommerce apps.
- Smart Product Categories: Extending Odoo's category model so subcategories automatically inherit technical data.
- Live Lead Times: Automatically pulling real-time customer lead times from inventory straight to the website frontend.
- Strict B2B2B Checkout: Changing the regular Odoo eCommerce checkout flow to enforce mandatory end-user address tracking.
- Automatic Data Flow: Letting product specifications automatically pass through complex nested subcategories.
Key Learnings:
- Why you should eliminate external eCommerce integrations by leveraging native Odoo Website architecture.
- How to extend Odoo category models to propagate complex technical data automatically.
- How to dynamically expose backend inventory lead times to the frontend customer experience.
- How to customize the Odoo checkout process to capture multi-tier reseller data, incl. end user information.
Target Audience:
Technical Sales Leads, Solutions Architects, Senior Python Devs, and Technical Leads using Odoo Enterprise v18 and onwards.

tracks.name: „From Readiness to Rollout: How Hinz&Kunzt Prepared a Complex ERP Transformation with Odoo“
tracks.speaker_line: Christiane Grothus, Managing Director at Opalis
tracks.description_html: Implementing a new ERP system is never just about software — especially not when long-established processes, specific organizational requirements and a complex operating model come together. In this session, Hinz&Kunzt, Opalis Consulting and Intero will jointly share how an Odoo project can be successfully prepared and launched when clarity, readiness and stakeholder alignment are just as important as the technical solution itself. The talk focuses on how an organization with a unique operating model can move towards a future-proof ERP platform. It highlights key thematic areas such as mapping core business processes in Odoo, addressing specific functional requirements, integrating relevant interfaces, preparing data migration, and setting up structured testing, training and project governance. These areas reflect the main functional project topics identified during the preparation phase. A particularly valuable angle of this story is the preparation phase before implementation: Opalis supported Hinz&Kunzt in shaping the transformation, moderating the selection process, preparing the organization from a change-management perspective and, after an unsuccessful first attempt with another Odoo partner, connecting the organization with Intero. This makes the session more than a software success story — it becomes a practical case about readiness, partner selection and the conditions required for successful ERP transformation. Attendees will gain actionable insights into the success factors of a more complex Odoo rollout, the interaction between organizational readiness and implementation, and the importance of setting up the right project foundations from the very beginning.

tracks.name: Unified Commerce with Odoo Enterprise: E-Commerce, PoS & Marketplace - All in One
tracks.speaker_line: Mi Dinh, Head of Commerce ERP at much. Consulting
tracks.description_html:
Retail has changed. Customers now expect a seamless experience across every sales channel. Whether they're browsing online, walking into a physical store, or shopping on a marketplace, the brand experience should remain consistent, fast, and efficient. This talk showcases how Odoo empowers businesses to unify their sales channels using E-Commerce, Point of Sale, and marketplace integrations within one single ERP system. We will demonstrate how out-of-the-box functionalities and ready integrations reduce time to market, lower operational complexity, and significantly cut costs. From first click to final sale, discover how Odoo can support a true omnichannel commerce strategy.

Key Points:

- How E-Commerce & PoS work seamlessly out of the box in Odoo Enterprise
- Leveraging Odoo to provide a unified customer experience across digital and physical channels
- Integrating with marketplaces like Amazon, eBay, and others using native and third-party apps
- Reducing operational complexity by centralizing products, inventory, and order processing
- Case examples from retail clients who went live faster and scaled smarter with Odoo

Key Learnings:

- Understanding the architectural advantages of Odoo's unified backend for omnichannel retail
- Strategies to reduce cost and time-to-go-live using standard Odoo features
- Best practices for managing inventory and fulfillment across multiple channels
- Insights into integrating marketplaces and automating order flows

Target Audience:

- Retail and E-Commerce Managers
- Digital Transformation Leads
- Business Owners planning omnichannel strategies

tracks.name: Re-Commerce at Scale With Odoo - Real-Time Retail Across 18 Stores and One Unified E-Commerce Experience
tracks.speaker_line: Kristian Gram Krogh & Diogo Duarte, CTO & CTO, Founder at Greenmind
tracks.description_html:
Re-commerce is booming, but it doesn’t play by traditional e-commerce rules. When every product is unique and inventory exists only once, availability becomes the biggest challenge. In this session, Martin Roulund from GreenMind and Diogo Duarte from ERPGAP share how GreenMind, Denmark’s leading retailer within Refurbished Electronics with 18 physical stores, successfully built a scalable re-commerce operation where online and offline work as one.

Discover how real-time stock synchronization across all stores enables GreenMind to sell confidently online and creates a seamless omnichannel experience, how intelligent order orchestration decides the best fulfillment location based on value and availability, and how Alokai powers a seamless e-commerce experience on top of a highly dynamic inventory model.

If you’re exploring circular economy, re-commerce, or complex omnichannel setups, this session will give you practical insights into turning operational complexity into a competitive advantage.

tracks.name: Wero - European sovereignty in digital payments
tracks.speaker_line: Alfredo Prieto Rodrigo, Director Business Acceptance at EPI Company
tracks.description_html:
I’m reaching out to propose a speaking session at Odoo event in Belgium, on one of the most defining shifts currently underway in European payments: the rise of Wero and what it means for sovereignty, innovation, and competition in Belgium and across Europe.

As the European Payments Initiative brings Wero to market, we are moving from concept to reality, building a truly European alternative for account-to-account payments that is scalable, secure, and designed for everyday use cases from P2P to e-commerce and in-store transactions.

A session on Wero would resonate strongly with your audience, particularly in Belgium, where the market is at a pivotal moment between established domestic habits and the emergence of new pan-European solutions. The discussion would go beyond product, focusing on:

- How Europe can reduce reliance on non-European payment schemes
- What Wero changes for banks, merchants, and consumers
- The role of instant payments and account-based rails in shaping the future
- Practical implications for the Belgian ecosystem and time-to-market considerations

The goal would be to provide a clear, candid perspective: what’s real today, what’s coming next, and where the industry needs to collaborate to make it succeed.

I’m confident this would not only add strategic value to your agenda but also spark meaningful discussion among participants navigating this transition.

Happy to share more details or tailor the session to your audience.

tracks.name: Empowering the Portal: Let Your Clients Self-Service and Save Your Team Time
tracks.speaker_line: Gin Yan, Business Advisor at Sodexis, Inc.
tracks.description_html:
Discover how to optimize Odoo’s customer portal to give your clients 24/7 access to their data, reducing administrative overhead and speeding up business cycles.

Your customer service and sales teams likely spend hours every week responding to routine emails. They are stuck sending copy-paste invoice PDFs, tracking down shipping numbers, or manually updating customers on order statuses. This back-and-forth slows your team down, and it forces your clients to wait on an email response just to get basic information about their own accounts.
We solve this bottleneck by leaning into Odoo’s native customer portal and tailoring it to act as a true self-service hub. Instead of treating the portal as an afterthought, we configure it so your clients can log in 24/7 to securely view their order history, download invoices, pay outstanding balances, and track shipments in real time. For businesses with recurring revenue models, we can even allow customers to manage their own subscriptions or submit support tickets directly through their dashboard, which automatically routes the data right into your Odoo backend.
Giving your clients direct access does not mean losing control. It simply removes the friction from the process. By shifting routine tasks to a secure self-service portal, you give your customers the instant answers they want while freeing up your team to focus on higher-value work.

tracks.name: Retail & Distribution Reimagined: Driving Performance with Odoo
tracks.speaker_line: Clémentine Cailleau from Metrum
tracks.description_html:
Retail and distribution companies face increasing pressure: tighter margins, rising customer expectations, growing operational complexity and the need to make faster decisions.

Odoo can do much more than digitalize existing processes. When implemented with the right functional approach, enhanced with targeted custom developments and empowered by AI, it becomes a true performance platform that creates measurable competitive advantage.

In this live demonstration, we will follow the journey of a retail and distribution company through its entire value chain, showcasing how Odoo supports every key business process—from purchasing and warehouse operations to sales, customer service and management decision-making.

Rather than focusing on individual modules, we will demonstrate how standard Odoo, carefully selected customizations and AI-powered capabilities work together to:

Optimize purchasing and replenishment decisions
Improve warehouse productivity and inventory accuracy
Increase sales efficiency across channels
Automate repetitive operational tasks
Deliver actionable insights through AI
Support managers with real-time performance indicators
Create sustainable competitive advantages while keeping the solution scalable and maintainable

The session will also explain the methodology behind these choices: when to leverage standard Odoo, when customization creates real business value, and where AI delivers tangible ROI rather than unnecessary complexity.

Attendees will leave with a practical framework for designing high-performance retail and distribution solutions that combine functional excellence, technology and business impact.

tracks.description_html:
Kentmaster has built meat-processing equipment for over 50 years, with operations across the United States, Australia, Ireland, South Africa, China, and Argentina. As the business scaled, NetSuite's rising licensing costs and limited flexibility became a real constraint, while quoting, manufacturing, and inventory ran across disconnected tools that slowed the business down.

This session walks through Kentmaster's migration from NetSuite to Odoo and the configure-to-order solution Aktiv built around it. We will cover the full journey: discovery and solution blueprinting, a large-scale data migration of thousands of products, variants, and complex BoMs with no disruption to operations, and a custom CPQ module tightly integrated with Sales and Manufacturing. The result is a single flow where a confirmed quote automatically generates the correct BoM and routes it to production, removing the rework and pricing inconsistencies that came from quoting outside the ERP.

Beyond CPQ, we will show how location-aware manufacturing, preferred-location inventory rules with serial traceability, and an automated order-to-cash flow came together into one connected system, giving leadership real-time visibility across multiple companies for the first time.

Attendees evaluating a migration from a costly proprietary ERP, or manufacturers struggling to connect quoting to production, will leave with a practical reference for how this is done on Odoo.

What attendees will learn:

- How to plan and execute a large-scale NetSuite-to-Odoo migration without disrupting live operations
- How CPQ can drive accurate quotes and automatic BoM creation straight into manufacturing
- How location-aware production and preferred-location inventory rules improve accuracy across multiple warehouses
- What a connected quote-to-production-to-invoice flow looks like in practice

tracks.name: Beyond Serial Numbers: Automating High-Volume Software Licensing in Odoo Enterprise.
tracks.speaker_line: Lisa Adamy, ERP Consultant at much. Consulting
tracks.description_html:
Software distributors face a unique structural paradox in Odoo: they require the traceability of serial numbers without the overhead of physical inventory moves. Arina, a leading European provider of digital forensics tools, struggled with a fragmented "Order-to-Cash" flow where license keys were manually copy-pasted across Sales Orders, Purchase Orders, and Subscriptions, leading to significant data decay and renewal leakage. To solve this, a centralized license.key architecture was deployed, leveraging Odoo Enterprise Subscription logic to create a persistent digital asset thread.

By inheriting standard Enterprise methods such as _prepare_invoice_line and _get_renew_upsell_values, the system ensures that license keys persist automatically through the entire lifecycle - from the initial RFQ to annual upsells. This deep integration allows for "Back-to-Back" procurement, where purchase prices are secured before Sales Order confirmation, a critical requirement for high-margin software distribution. The result is a 80% reduction in administrative overhead, managing over 1,000 active subscriptions with zero manual data duplication between procurement and accounting.

In this talk, we will cover:

- Digital Asset Centralization: Why standard stock.production.lot fails for intangible goods and how to replace it.
- Subscription Persistence: Using license_key_ids to maintain traceability during Odoo Enterprise renewal and upsell cycles.
- Automated Procurement Flow: Triggering RFQs via custom product flags to secure margins before SO confirmation.
- The Mixin Architecture: Deploying license.key.mixin to unify headers and lines across SO, PO, and Invoicing.
- Reporting & Transparency: Dynamic injection of license data into PDF templates for quotes, invoices, and delivery slips.
- Order-to-Cash Efficiency: Reducing manual intervention by 70% for complex forensic software distribution.

You will learn:

- How to manage non-storable assets that require unique identifiers without triggering stock moves.
- How to extend Odoo Enterprise Subscription logic to carry custom relational data into upsell and renewal orders.
- How to automate the "Back-to-Back" vendor procurement process for services and digital goods.
- How to avoid data silos by using a single source of truth for license expiration and payment dates.
- How to architect a modular Mixin that ensures consistent data flow across all accounting documents.

Target Audience:

- Odoo Partners & Consultants managing software or SaaS distribution clients.
- CFOs & Operations Managers using Odoo Enterprise Subscriptions.
- Intermediate Developers interested in extending Subscription and Procurement logic (v18/v19).

tracks.name: Multi-Company and Multi-Country Consolidations in Odoo 19
tracks.speaker_line: Cecilie Barreto, Director of Implementation at Sodexis, Inc.
tracks.description_html:
Are you struggling to manage financial consolidations across multiple entities and currencies?

Would you prefer a seamless, automated way to aggregate your financial data when closing the fiscal year across different countries, while ensuring compliance with varying local regulations?

Enter Odoo V19! Odoo’s latest localization and accounting enhancements enable seamless real-time data synchronization across borders, thereby solving the complex multi-company and multi-country consolidation problem for expanding businesses.

This technology eliminates the need for manual spreadsheets and tedious external reporting tools. Over the past years, our team has successfully streamlined complex international accounting structures, enabling financial departments to reduce their closing times. With Odoo 19’s advanced multi-currency revaluation and centralized dashboard, multi-national groups can now manage dozens of legal entities with full transparency and compliance.

Join this session to discover how growing enterprises have achieved remarkable efficiency in their global operations—and how Odoo 19’s newest consolidation features play a key role in reaching these milestones.

Representing Sodexis will be Cecilie Barreto, our Director of Implementation.

Since 2012, Sodexis has been a full-service Odoo Implementation Partner, with a Consulting and Development team focused on maximizing customers’ ROI and user experience. Sodexis is one of the longest-tenured implementation Odoo Partners in the US and also has a presence in Switzerland, France, and Austria. Sodexis brings a wealth of experience and valuable expertise to its clients, having successfully implemented over 150 projects and built hundreds of custom applications. More info: https://sodexis.com/

tracks.name: Automating 30,000 Members: Translating Complex NPO Fee Matrices into Odoo Enterprise Subscriptions
tracks.speaker_line: Nicolas Colsman, CEO at ZdoV GmbH
tracks.description_html:
Managing a 30,000-member association in Germany traditionally mandates heavy administrative overhead, particularly when membership dues are dictated by convoluted variables like academic degrees, membership tenure, and specialized research grants. Historically, processing these nested logic trees required legacy databases, fractured Excel sheets, and 2.5 full-time equivalents (FTEs) purely dedicated to billing and reconciliation.

To eliminate this bottleneck, ZdoV architected a centralized association framework utilizing Odoo Enterprise Contacts, Subscriptions, and Accounting. We developed custom calculation logic to inherit the intricate legacy fee matrix and map it directly onto dynamic Odoo subscription products. This architecture programmatically executes the entire financial lifecycle: it calculates the precise variable fee per member, automates recurring invoicing, processes high-volume SEPA Direct Debit mandates natively within the accounting module, and generates legally compliant German donation receipts (Spendenbescheinigungen) without manual intervention.

By replacing disconnected legacy systems with a unified Odoo Enterprise environment, the association fundamentally restructured its operational efficiency. The automated billing and SEPA reconciliation cycle reduced the required administrative overhead from 2.5 FTEs down to a 0.5 FTE workload, proving Odoo's capacity to handle massive, highly localized non-profit constraints.

Key Points of this Talk:
- Mapping legacy variable fee matrices (academic degrees, grants) to Odoo Subscriptions.
- Centralizing 30,000 member records within Odoo Enterprise Contacts to deprecate Excel.
- Executing high-volume SEPA Direct Debit mandates via Odoo Enterprise Accounting.
- Automating the generation of compliant German donation receipts (Spendenbescheinigungen).
- Reducing billing administration workload from 2.5 to 0.5 FTEs.

Key Learnings:

- How to translate intricate legacy calculation parameters into dynamic Odoo subscription products.
- How to configure Odoo Accounting for high-volume, automated SEPA reconciliation.
- How to structure Odoo Contacts to handle complex non-profit membership hierarchies.

Target Audience:

Functional Consultants, NPO Administrators, and Solution Architects using Odoo Enterprise.

tracks.name: Customer success story: Artel Rubber's Engineer-to-Order Transformation with Odoo
tracks.speaker_line: Giovanni Ughi, CEO at BRYO GmbH
tracks.description_html:
In this talk, the CEO of Bryo shares the story of the digital transformation at Artel Rubber, the UK’s leading manufacturer of silicon hoses for complex industrial applications. This is not a standard ERP implementation story, but a journey through complexity, failed attempts, and a breakthrough enabled by Odoo.

Artel Rubber operates in an engineer-to-order environment, where every product is designed and manufactured based on customer requirements. This creates a high level of complexity in one of the most critical business processes: designing, quoting and manufacturing custom products.

The key challenge is to define a new bill of materials within the ERP system for each new design. Each bill of materials includes different operations distributed across six work centres and consists of multiple components and raw materials.

For years, this challenge blocked migration to a modern ERP system. Operations were distributed across four custom legacy systems and paper-based processes dating back to the 1990s. A previous ERP migration project ran for four years, costing hundreds of thousands of euros, but failed.

By building on Odoo's standard manufacture-to-order workflows, Bryo delivered a fully integrated solution in just three months across all key modules: sales, manufacturing, shop floor, inventory, purchasing and invoicing. The key to this success was a deep understanding of the customers’ proprietary engineering tools and creating a simple connection to the Manufacturing module. This achieved a 20% efficiency gain in back-office operations within the first three months, alongside improved planning and delivery performance.

Attendees will learn how Odoo can successfully support complex engineer-to-order manufacturers, the importance of understanding customer-specific processes, and the implementation strategies that enabled a project previously considered too complex to become a successful digital transformation.

This session demonstrates how Odoo can become the backbone of even highly complex manufacturing operations when implemented with the right approach.

tracks.name: One CRM, one source of truth: How a publishing company consolidated a fragmented customer landscape on Odoo – and powered its print-to-digital shift
tracks.speaker_line: Lars Schymonski from Ruhrdot
tracks.description_html: media magneten, a publishing and advertising company in Essen, ran its sales on a fragmented landscape: SAP as the master-data backbone, a home-grown legacy system for orders and field service, and a scatter of point tools. Customer data lived everywhere and nowhere - no single view, constant manual re-entry between systems, and limited control over their own data. Together with ruhrdot., they made Odoo 19 the operational heart of the business: one CRM as the single source of truth for roughly 200,000 customer records, with SAP retained as the system of record. The result is a 360° customer view, sales workflows freed from manual re-entry and media breaks, advisor-specific marketing automation through Brevo, and trigger-based sales steering that tells advisors who to contact and when. Just as important, the project restored media magneten's sovereignty over its own customer data and laid the operational foundation for its strategic shift from print to digital. Instead of a big-bang cutover, ruhrdot. delivered a disciplined six-month MVP with a phased, pilot-first go-live. This talk shows how a mid-market company turns a CRM migration into a genuine business transformation.

tracks.name: Scaling a luxury retailer across five countries on Odoo
tracks.speaker_line: Ruben Van den broecke + Egbert Van Sande (DOL), Project manager at Dynapps
tracks.description_html:
How do you grow a premium lifestyle brand across five countries, with Cuban cigars in one window and online auctions in the next, all running on a single platform?
That is the bet Dominique London is making. What started as a small shop in Ghent has grown into a multi-country retailer spanning Belgium, the UK, Switzerland, Luxembourg and the Canary Islands, with physical boutiques, a B2C webshop, a POS network, and a UK-grown online auction business. To support that ambition, the company chose Odoo as the single backbone for commerce, POS, inventory and accounting.
In this session, Dominique London and Dynapps share what it takes to make that work in practice. We zoom in on the architectural choices behind a multi-company, multi-country setup where one Odoo website automatically serves the right prices, products, VAT treatment and currency based on the visitor's location. We look at how strict assortment rules are handled at storefront and checkout level.
We also share the lessons that won't make the brochure: where standard Odoo simply works, where it doesn't, and which compromises pay off when you are racing toward a growth target.
Whether you run a multi-brand retailer, are about to launch in a second country, or are skeptical that a single ERP can carry both a luxury experience and a complex backend, this session gives you a practical look at how it is done.

tracks.name: Building Freight Forwarding Depth on a Flexible Odoo ERP Foundation
tracks.speaker_line: Devashish Patyal, Deputy CEO at ICS Global
tracks.description_html:
Freight forwarding companies rarely struggle because they lack basic ERP features; they struggle because their operations require deeper control beyond standard sales, invoicing, accounting, and inventory flows. A freight business needs connected processes for enquiries, quotations, bookings, shipments, containers, House and Master Bills of Lading, buying and selling rates, margin visibility, document generation, customer updates, customs, manifests, and country-specific compliance.

This session will share how a flexible Odoo ERP foundation can be shaped into a freight forwarding operating platform by adding logistics-specific workflows, structured data models, operational checkpoints, integration readiness, and scalable controls. The presentation will cover the practical journey from generic business processes to domain-ready logistics operations, including shipment lifecycle management, rate management, documentation, invoicing, dashboards, and multi-country process design.

The key takeaways for the audience will include how to identify domain gaps during discovery, avoid unnecessary over-customization, design freight workflows with long-term scalability, and build industry depth while preserving the flexibility of the Odoo platform. This session will be valuable for Odoo consultants, ERP implementation teams, logistics companies, solution architects, and business leaders planning digital transformation in freight forwarding and logistics operations.

tracks.name: Populate, Odoo's new data generation framework
tracks.speaker_line: Victor Piryns, Performance Engineer at Odoo
tracks.description_html:
Generating realistic Odoo databases for development, demonstrations, and performance testing has traditionally required custom scripts and considerable maintenance.

Populate introduces a new declarative framework for generating large, coherent datasets directly in Odoo. In this talk, we will explore how blueprints, generators, relationships, statistical distributions, scaling, and parallel execution work together to produce realistic data efficiently. We will also look behind the scenes at the framework’s architecture and see how developers can extend it for their own modules and use cases.

tracks.name: How to recruit Gen Z (without being cringe)
tracks.speaker_line: Elise Derclaye & Kaat Goiris from Odoo
tracks.description_html:
Recruitment is a bit like dating.

You wouldn't propose on the first date. So why do companies expect students to commit before they've even had the chance to get to know them?

And just like dating, first impressions matter - but eventually, the real you has to show up.

At Odoo, we've been exploring what happens when recruitment starts long before the application : when students get the chance to meet the people, experience the culture, and make up their own minds about whether there could be a match.

Join us as we share what we've tried, what we've learned, and what happens when you stop trying to convince Gen Z - and start letting them discover you instead.

tracks.name: Draw Your Ideas. Make Them Stick.
tracks.speaker_line: Dorbolo, SKETCHNOTING trainings at Pictobello.com - Denis Dorbolo
tracks.description_html:
Most business ideas are forgotten minutes after they're shared.

In this fast-paced and interactive session, you'll discover how simple sketches can make ideas clearer, conversations more engaging, and messages more memorable. Through a few playful exercises, you'll experience the power of sketchnoting for yourself—even if you think you can't draw.

Whether you're leading meetings, presenting to clients, brainstorming with a team, or simply looking for a fresh way to communicate, visual thinking can open new possibilities. This workshop offers a fun first step into the world of sketchnoting and visual communication.

You'll leave with a different perspective on how ideas can be shared, understood, and remembered—and perhaps with the surprising realization that drawing is far more accessible than you ever imagined.

Who should attend?
Entrepreneurs, managers, consultants, team leaders, trainers, and curious professionals who want to communicate with greater clarity and impact.

tracks.name: From AI CPQ to Shop Floor: Connecting HIPE to Odoo for the Packaging Industry
tracks.speaker_line: Sébastien BOSSOUTROT, co-Founder and co-CEO at IROKOO
tracks.description_html:
In the packaging industry, every order is unique. Dimensions, materials, printing, finishing: nothing is a standard catalog product. Yet most converters still quote these orders either in spreadsheets or in legacy ERPs that were never designed to handle configurable products. Margin only becomes clear after production. The configurator, when there is one, lives outside the ERP, so the gap between what was sold and what is produced gets filled manually, slowly, and with costly errors.

This talk shows, live in Odoo 19 (20), how an AI-powered CPQ built for packaging (HIPE) connects directly to Odoo to close that gap, end to end. HIPE owns the front of the funnel, configuration and AI-assisted quoting. The moment a quote is won, Odoo takes over the entire ERP backbone: the sales order, the cascading bill of materials, the purchase needs for materials and subcontracting, the manufacturing order, inventory, accounting, and a reliable cost, with no double entry. We walk the full path: from the configured quote in HIPE, to procurement and the shop floor, to inventory and margin analysis in Odoo.

We also share what it takes to make this integration reliable in real operations: keeping both systems in sync, handling errors gracefully, and turning a complex configured product into an accurate, multi-level bill of materials. Key takeaway: a concrete blueprint to turn Odoo into the backbone of configure-to-order manufacturing, with packaging as the showcase but lessons that apply to any made-to-order business.

tracks.name: From Sage, Satelix & PrestaShop to Odoo: How Toulet Medical Unified Its Distribution Business Across Stores & E-commerce
tracks.speaker_line: Séphora DAYNE MOREAU, CEO at GS CONSEILS
tracks.description_html:
Toulet Medical is one of the medical equipment distributors on Réunion Island, a French overseas territory located in the Indian Ocean. The company serves healthcare professionals, medical institutions, care facilities, and private customers through multiple physical stores, warehouses, and complementary e-commerce websites.

Before Odoo, Toulet Medical relied on several separate solutions, including Sage for business management and accounting, PrestaShop for e-commerce, and additional tools used to support daily operations. As the company continued to grow, managing sales, inventory, purchasing, logistics, customer service, and online sales across multiple systems became increasingly complex, time-consuming, and costly.

To support its development, Toulet Medical decided to centralize its operations within Odoo and transform its information system into a single integrated platform. Today, Odoo is used to manage sales, purchasing, inventory, logistics, accounting, customer service, physical stores, and the Toulet Medical and Couches & Co e-commerce websites.

During this session, we will share the company’s digital transformation journey and explain how Odoo became the backbone of its operations.

Attendees will discover how the company successfully migrated from multiple disconnected applications to a unified ERP platform while preparing for future growth.

The presentation will also highlight the specific challenges of operating a medical equipment distribution company on Réunion Island, including import lead times, stock availability, multi-site operations, managing two brands and two e-commerce websites within the same company, multi-company environments, retail store operations, and the high level of customer service required in the healthcare sector.

Key Takeaways

* Successfully migrating from Sage and PrestaShop to Odoo.
* Centralizing sales, purchasing, inventory, accounting, and e-commerce within a single platform.
* Managing multiple stores and warehouses efficiently.
* Operating multiple e-commerce websites from a single database.
* Improving inventory visibility and replenishment processes.
* Supporting business growth through standardized and scalable processes.
* Lessons learned from a real-world implementation project on Réunion Island.

Value for the Audience

This session will provide a practical and transparent customer success story from a real-life digital transformation project. Participants will gain insights into the challenges encountered, the benefits achieved, and the lessons learned while replacing multiple business applications with a fully integrated ERP system.

Attendees will leave with concrete ideas and best practices that can be applied to their own organizations, whether they manage distribution operations, retail networks, e-commerce businesses, or multi-site companies.

Target Audience

* Business owners and executives
* Operations managers
* Supply chain and logistics managers
* Purchasing managers
* E-commerce managers
* Finance and accounting managers
* IT managers
* Odoo partners and consultants
* Distribution and retail companies looking to centralize their operations within a single platform

Additional Information

The session would ideally be presented in French. Presentation materials can be provided in English if required, but presenting in French would allow the speakers to be more comfortable during discussions and audience Q&A sessions.

tracks.name: 4 Lifestyle Brands, 7 E-commerce Channels, 1 Odoo: Migrating a Group off Sage Without Overselling
tracks.speaker_line: Nico Ziemski from ruhrdot GmbH
tracks.description_html: Zeitgeist GmbH runs four consumer lifestyle brands (the watch brands Detomaso, Yves Camani and Lilienthal plus Kooja) across direct-to-consumer Shopify stores and the Amazon and Otto marketplaces, with e-commerce as the group's core business. Their legacy Sage ERP modeled stock as components and bills of materials, which created a constant overselling risk and tied up a large block of component inventory that blocked a clean transition. ruhrdot. replaced Sage with a single Odoo 19 Enterprise instance for the entire group: two legal entities in one multi-company setup, a simplified single-SKU inventory model, and separate DATEV exports per entity for German accounting compliance. Odoo sits at the hub of the supply chain, orchestrating four Shopify stores through a custom connector, the Amazon and Otto channels through a middleware, and fulfillment through third-party logistics via a SOAP integration that also routes watch engraving. Instead of a big-bang cutover, we went live brand by brand, month by month, so learnings from the first brand fed the next. This talk shows how to design a multi-brand group ERP from day one, retire a risky legacy inventory model, and de-risk a large migration through phased go-lives.

tracks.name: Success story from the association Groupement des Campeurs Universitaires (GCU) on the migration from Odoo version 12 to Odoo version 18: a project that now enables the association to manage its 88 campgrounds—run by its volunteer members throughout France—in a unified, shared environment
tracks.speaker_line: MARTINEZ Philippe & Noémie Keller, Vice Président & Director of Operations
tracks.description_html:
Operating a campsite depends on many factors, and this challenge takes on a special
significance for the GCU, which has 88 campsites located throughout France, run by volunteer members, and requiring a coordinated organizational structure while preserving the autonomy of each campsite.
This project, presented jointly by the GCU and Sodexis, is a testament to their collaborative efforts toward a shared goal: to upgrade the GCU’s information system to better meet its needs while preserving the unique characteristics of its nonprofit model.
As part of the migration from Odoo v12 to Odoo v18, one of the major challenges was to make the most of Odoo’s native features in order to align more closely with the standard, while reducing dependence on the numerous custom developments that had been implemented in the previous version. The goal was not to replicate the existing system exactly, but to rethink the processes to find the best balance between Odoo’s capabilities, business needs, and the specific operational requirements of the GCU.
Sodexis supported the GCU in this process overhaul to optimize the processes and integrate them into Odoo v18. However, some existing workflows were closely tied to the GCU’s association-based operations and the autonomy granted to volunteers in the day-to-day management of the campsites. The project therefore required in-depth consideration to balance standardization and automation with respect for this human-centered, decentralized model. The project made it possible to rebuild the GCU’s main business workflows—from member enrollment to the multi-site self-management of reservations for campsites and rental units—while implementing specific connectors with external partners, notably insurance services (Xplorassur) and French payment solutions such as ANCV – Chèques-Vacances Connect.
The challenge was twofold: to ensure maximum accounting transparency and to enable the GCU to be fully operational on Odoo in time for the start of the 2026 season. Goal achieved. Today, the GCU’s Odoo platform has recorded more than 8,300 confirmed stay reservations, 300 insurance purchase orders, 4,000 support tickets resolved through a system that distributes requests among different teams, and 30,500 invoices generated directly in Odoo, with only a limited number of special cases or anomalies.
This case study illustrates Odoo’s ability to support a complex organizational model, while demonstrating that a successful migration depends as much on technology as it does on a thorough understanding of the organization’s workflows, processes, and specific characteristics.

tracks.name: Scaling Odoo for Complex Retail: Dreambaby’s Journey Across 30+ Stores, a Central DC and Tailor-made applications
tracks.speaker_line: Daan Sileghem, Founder, Managing Partner at Konu BV
tracks.description_html:
Dreambaby, the largest baby retail brand in Belgium, runs its core operation on Odoo. With more than 260 employees, 30+ physical stores (with additional stores planned for 2026), and a central warehouse, Odoo serves as the daily backbone for all core business processes.
The platform covers accounting, inventory, purchasing, sales, POS, HR, planning, attendance, customer service, and more, all within one centralised system. Despite numerous integrations with external systems, including marketing platforms, Shopify eCommerce, and Power BI, Odoo serves as the single source of truth (SSOT) for all operational and master data.

As Odoo partner Konu from Kortrijk, Belgium, we delivered the full implementation under a very ambitious timeline. Dreambaby migrated from SAP to Odoo and went live in just 8 months, followed by a hypercare phase of about 3 months, without disrupting ongoing operations.

While Odoo’s standard applications provided a strong foundation, Dreambaby’s retail-specific complexity required deep customisation across multiple core flows, including accounting, HR, POS, purchasing, sales, helpdesk, and more.

Inventory and logistics were heavily extended to match Dreambaby’s scale and complexity. Odoo manages 30+ stores in a multi-branch routing setup, with store replenishment driven by over one million replenishment rules. Store assortments are dynamically defined through a custom store range management application, powered by a bespoke sales forecasting tool. The platform supports advanced eCommerce flows, dynamic picking and prioritisation (for giftlists, online orders, and other channels), and online shipping directly from stores.

On top of the core platform, we developed a suite of custom-built applications tailored to Dreambaby’s business:
- A bespoke Giftlist (Birthlist) engine built in Odoo with a headless React frontend
- A custom loyalty program, deeply integrated with both POS and webshop
- A store replenishment engine with dynamic demand forecasting
- Automated shelf label printing driven by real-time pricing
- A dynamic price display system for managing in-store and online promotions

Today, we continue to support Dreambaby on a daily basis, driving its ongoing digital transformation with fast-paced improvements to the giftlist, loyalty program, and overall shop concept. This is an ongoing journey, part of a broader conceptual modernisation of the Dreambaby retail experience. The roadmap focuses on evolving the tailor-made applications and strengthening employee-facing tools and interfaces, with a clear emphasis on improving both customer and employee experiences.

This session offers an honest and practical account of the project: what worked well, where we encountered friction, and what we would approach differently. It is ideal for teams considering Odoo for full operational coverage in a complex retail environment.

tracks.name: From clicks to bricks: Create an omnichannel shopping experience with Odoo
tracks.speaker_line: Claire Almiñana San Felix from Odoo
tracks.description_html:
What if your online store, your physical checkout, your warehouse, and every sales channel you operate could all speak the same language, in real time?
In this talk, we'll walk through how modern retail is no longer about choosing between online and offline, but about building a unified shopping experience where every touchpoint feeds every other. We'll explore how Odoo connects your eCommerce storefront, Point of Sale, Inventory, and other sales channels into a single, living system, where a sale made in-store instantly updates your online stock, a product listed on Google Shopping reflects your latest pricing, and your warehouse always knows what to prepare next.
No more data silos. No more manual syncs. No more "sorry, that item shows available online but we're actually out."
Whether you're a retailer taking your first steps into digital, or a digital-native brand opening your first physical location, this session will show you what it really takes to deliver a seamless customer experience

tracks.name: Casa Lopez & Tissus Choisis – Digitalizing Retail Operations with Odoo
tracks.speaker_line: Valentine Burnay, Project Manager at Eezee-IT
tracks.description_html:
Casa Lopez and Tissus Choisis, two iconic Parisian houses known for their colourful, Mediterranean-inspired style under the artistic direction of Pierre Sauvage, undertook a digital transformation of their retail operations, moving from a heavily paper-based, poorly integrated system to a unified digital platform with Odoo, covering purchasing, point of sale, sales, and inventory, integrated with a WMS for a 360° in-store customer experience.
Implemented across 2 boutiques for 10 users in just 3 months, the project required tight planning and a pragmatic approach to scoping, configuration, and change management to meet an ambitious timeline while fitting the realities of a small, high-end retail team.
The session will share how the team approached process redesign, POS and inventory optimization, the Odoo-WMS integration, and user adoption within a short timeframe, along with practical lessons learned for similar retail transformations.

Key takeaways:
Moving from paper and disconnected tools to an integrated digital platform.

Best practices for POS, sales, and inventory management with Odoo in retail.
- Integrating Odoo with a WMS for streamlined stock management.
- Designing a 360° in-store customer experience.
- Change management for fast, small-scale implementations.
- Target audience: Retail managers, project managers, IT managers, business analysts, and executives involved in retail digital transformation projects.

tracks.speaker_line: Nils Goossens Bara, Business Analyst at Odoo
tracks.description_html:
Optimizing the Checkout Process in Odoo

Building an efficient checkout process requires a clear understanding of how Odoo manages the final steps of a sale. This live demonstration walks you through the system's real-time behavior, starting with the core distinction between backend payment providers and customer-facing payment methods. Next, we will compare the operational workflows of manual delivery setups versus automated external shipper integrations. Finally, we will explore the latest Odoo updates that allow customers to select their preferred delivery dates and time slots directly during checkout.

tracks.name: Synchronizing Odoo instances in Crisis Zones: a distributed architecture supporting Emergency's mission
tracks.speaker_line: Andrea Colangelo, CTO at Andrea Colangelo
tracks.description_html:
Emergency operates in war zones and low-resource settings where internet connectivity is unreliable or absent. Yet, they need a robust information system to manage hospitals and field clinics efficiently. In this talk, we will present how we designed and implemented a distributed architecture to synchronize multiple local Odoo instances with a central server, ensuring data consistency while respecting the operational constraints of Emergency’s field missions.

We will cover the key architectural choices we made to handle connectivity dropouts, conflict resolution, and secure data transfer, as well as the practical challenges faced while deploying and maintaining Odoo in environments with frequent power outages and network instability.

Beyond the humanitarian context, this distributed architecture has valuable applications wherever reliable connectivity cannot be guaranteed—such as in remote construction sites, maritime operations, or mobile field services—demonstrating how Odoo can ensure operational continuity even in the most challenging conditions.

****
N.B.: This is the same talk I was supposed to give at Odoo Experience 2025, but had to skip due to a health issue and never delivered. The version I would like to present this year includes some updates based on how the project has evolved over the last 10 months.
***

tracks.name: From Website to Business System: Moving Beyond Plugin Sprawl with Odoo
tracks.speaker_line: Colm Lynam, CEO at Combined Media Company
tracks.description_html:
Many growing businesses start by adding functionality to their website: eCommerce, events, memberships, online payments, forms, bookings, email marketing, CRM plugins and more. This works well at first, but over time the website can become a patchwork of disconnected tools, duplicated data and manual processes.

In this session, Combined Media will share how a digital agency’s work with websites naturally evolved into Odoo ERP delivery. We will explore the point at which businesses outgrow plugin-based operations, and how Odoo can provide a connected system across website, eCommerce, events, CRM, sales, inventory, accounting and customer management.

The talk will cover practical examples of common plugin-led workflows, the problems they create as businesses scale, and a phased approach to moving from a website-centred setup to a full Odoo business system. Attendees will leave with a clear framework for identifying when a business is ready to move beyond website plugins and how to approach that transition successfully.

Ozanimart is a toy wholesaler serving wholesale buyers who need bulk ordering, tiered pricing, and account-based access.

This is a very unique functionality for all those businesses who have lots of customers and don't want to increase the costing. They want to keep the licensing cost limited.

This session is aimed at Odoo partners, implementers, and businesses evaluating how to auto pilot distribution business and giving access to the businesses.

tracks.name: Odev meets AI : Automating Odoo development end-to-end
tracks.speaker_line: Sébastien Andreatta from Odoo
tracks.description_html:
odev is the CLI Odoo developers already reach for daily: it spins up a database on any Odoo version, manages worktrees and git branches per task, handles venvs and dependencies, runs the server, runs the tests, and generally removes the boilerplate around working with Odoo source. What it didn't do — until now — is write the code for you.

This talk shows how we plugged AI agents (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot, OpenCode) directly into that existing workflow. Instead of bolting AI on as a separate tool, odev uses the environment it already manages — the right Odoo version, the right worktree, a running database — as the context an AI agent needs to actually get work done: analyzing a task, scaffolding the module, running it, testing it, and iterating against real failures instead of hallucinated ones.

We'll do a live, end-to-end demo: starting from a bare task description, watch odev set up the dev environment and hand it off to an AI agent that scaffolds, runs, and tests a real Odoo module — then talk through what worked, what broke, and the design decisions behind wiring AI into a tool developers already trust for the unglamorous plumbing of Odoo development.

tracks.name: Still building your eCommerce website on Shopify? We need to talk
tracks.speaker_line: Lina Eweis from Odoo
tracks.description_html:
Showcase a few of our frontend "wow" factors (snippets and new features), while highlighting our backend integration edge, since everything connects natively to the other Odoo modules. 
Contrast this with the drawbacks of building on Shopify:

  1. You need external apps for everything, even basic features require third-party apps.
  2. Once you edit your Shopify website, it no longer receives theme updates. In Odoo, customizations are just snippets, and updates can still be forced.
  3. You can't just add a new feature. On Shopify, that often means hosting your own backend somewhere else and integrating it externally, which requires a developer. In Odoo, almost everything you need is already integrated.
  4. Shopify's checkout isn't customizable at all, and it isn't even part of your actual website.
  5. Return management is a pain, handled entirely by unofficial third-party apps. Here I'll showcase our new return management feature as the counterpoint.
  6. Shopify takes a percentage of your sales. We don't.

tracks.name: Beyond the Website Builder: Building Headless and Custom Interfaces on Odoo
tracks.speaker_line: Guillaume Roisin, CEO at Sigmagency SRL
tracks.description_html:
Summary
Most companies treat Odoo as a back-office and stop there. But Odoo is also the backend behind every interface your customers, partners and field teams actually touch custom portals, headless web and mobile apps, even offline-first tools for people working with no connection.
For years these architectures were expensive and reserved for ambitious projects. AI just changed the economics: the plumbing is cheap now, so far more projects can justify a custom front-end on top of Odoo. But the hard part didn't disappear it moved. The challenge is no longer can you build it, it's can you architect it so your data stays trustworthy.
In this talk we'll show what's possible beyond the standard Odoo website, when to go custom versus when to stay standard, and the architecture rules that keep one source of truth no matter how custom the interface gets with real examples in production.
Description
The standard Odoo website is excellent, and for most projects it should be the default. But some businesses need more than a theme can deliver: a customer portal with bespoke workflows, a native mobile app, a public platform at scale, or a tool their field teams can use with no internet at all.
The usual reflex is to bolt on a separate system and instantly recreate the data silos and manual reconciliation everyone is trying to escape. There's a better way: keep Odoo as the single source of truth for orders, inventory, accounting and CRM, and build the interface as a headless front-end that talks to Odoo as its backend. The result is a best-in-class user experience and full operational integration, you no longer have to choose.
What's new in 2026 is the economics. AI collapses the cost of the plumbing: the boilerplate, the API glue, the type generation from Odoo models, the sync scaffolding. Projects that weren't viable two years ago are viable today, and the market for custom interfaces is expanding fast. But that's also the trap: far more teams will now attempt these architectures without knowing where the landmines are. AI answers "can you build it." It does not answer "can you architect it so the data stays reliable." That judgment is the whole game.
In clear, practical terms, we'll cover:

The decision framework : how to tell whether a project belongs on the standard Odoo website or warrants a custom/headless interface, and the honest trade-offs in cost, time and maintainability. Standard should win more often than you'd think.
Odoo as a backend, not just a back-office : treating Odoo's data and business logic as the API core for any interface, so there's one source of truth no matter how custom the front-end gets.
Three faces of the custom front-end, one Odoo backend : the customer-facing product at scale (a headless platform serving 200k+ catalog items on Odoo), the partner/bespoke portal (custom React front-ends), and the hardest one: the offline-first field tool, where agents work with no connection, with sync and conflict resolution feeding everything straight back into Odoo.
The rules that keep it sane : where business logic must live (in Odoo, never in the front-end), how to handle auth, performance, offline sync and data integrity. The exact rules AI makes more critical, not less.
What this unlocks for your business : bespoke customer and partner experiences, mobile and field operations, and ambitious digital products, while every transaction still flows straight into Odoo.

By the end, you'll know what Odoo is truly capable of as the backbone of any digital product, when to stay standard and when to go custom and why, in the AI era, the value has shifted from writing the code to architecting it right.

tracks.name: Odoolingo: Learn Odoo and Languages at the Same Time!
tracks.speaker_line: Javier Colmeiro Aznar, Software Engineer in Customer Care at Braintec
tracks.description_html:
What happens when you mix a passion for Odoo with the addictive learning mechanics of Duolingo? You get Odoolingo—a gamified learning app built entirely using Odoo’s OWL framework and native backend translation engines.

This talk showcases a unique pet project, "vibecoded" during spare time, that turns Odoo's massive localization dataset into an interactive educational tool. Users can configure custom "courses" by selecting a source and target language. The app then dynamically scrapes and structures terms directly from native Odoo menu items, main forms, and views to generate real-time, short quizzes.

Key takeaways from this session include:

Creative Data Use: How to leverage Odoo’s native translation architecture (ir.translation) for non-traditional, gamified use cases.

OWL in Action: Building a highly reactive, state-driven, interactive UI entirely within the OWL framework.

Rapid Prototyping: Lessons learned from "vibecoding" a fully functional proof-of-concept from scratch.

Come see how this project was brought to life, explore the versatility of OWL for standalone mini-apps, and discover how to unlock the hidden potential of Odoo's internal terms!

tracks.name: Vivre sa passion avant de la penser : comment on devient entrepreneur sans l’avoir décidé ?
tracks.speaker_line: Inoxtag, Créateur de contenu
tracks.description_html:
Vidéaste, créateur de contenu, producteur, entrepreneur, Ines Benazzouz, alias Inoxtag, réunit près de 30 millions d’abonnés sur l’ensemble de ses plateformes.
Avec Kaizen, son documentaire sur l’ascension de l’Everest, il a bousculé les codes de l’audiovisuel français : sorti au cinéma, diffusé en plateforme, repris à la télévision et disponible sur YouTube, le film a franchi toutes les frontières que le secteur croyait étanches. Rien de tout cela ne figurait dans un plan. Inoxtag a simplement suivi ses projets jusqu’au bout. C’est ce chemin qu’il vient raconter : celui d’un autodidacte pour qui se lancer a toujours précédé le fait de savoir faire.

tracks.speaker_line: Maureen O'Hare, Partnerships Manager at 42 Belgium
tracks.description_html: As AI transforms the way software is built, many predict the decline of the software developer. The reality is the opposite. In this session, we'll explore why AI is elevating—not replacing—the role of developers, shifting them from writing code to designing systems, making architectural decisions, and solving increasingly complex problems. Drawing on industry trends and real-world examples, we'll discuss how the most valuable developers of the future will combine technical expertise with critical thinking, collaboration, and adaptability, and why investing in this new generation of tech talent is more important than ever.

tracks.name: From Farm to Export: Digitizing a 35-Year-Old Agri-Exporter's Multi-Country Operations
tracks.speaker_line: Purav Gandhi, Chief Executive Officer at Aspire Softserv
tracks.description_html:
For over three decades, a fruits-and-vegetables processor and exporter ran farm sourcing, cold-chain processing, and export documentation on disconnected spreadsheets and manual registers. As the business expanded sales and distribution into Europe, that fragility became a growth blocker: no real-time visibility between the production entity and the European sales office, no traceability from farmer intake to finished export pallet, and reporting cycles that took days to consolidate across entities and currencies.
As the implementing Odoo partner, Aspire Softserv consolidated the company's farm-to-export chain onto Odoo: a multi-company architecture connecting the production and European sales entities, Manufacturing with full batch traceability and HACCP-aligned quality checkpoints, Inventory with cold-storage zone tracking, and Accounting handling multi-currency and VAT consolidation. Cross-entity financial reporting dropped from couple of days to few minutes, and the business gained full yield and waste visibility for the first time.

tracks.name: Building custom Website and E-commerce with Odoo and why you should too
tracks.speaker_line: Guillaume Roisin, CEO at Sigmagency SRL
tracks.description_html:
SUMMARY

Most agencies build websites and e-commerce platforms disconnected from business operations, forcing companies to manage data in silos. 

In this talk, we will explain why using Odoo as the backbone for websites and e-commerce ecosystems is the best way to scale while reducing manual work and operational complexity. We will share what this shift means for your business and how it can transform your digital presence into a growth engine. 

DESCRIPTION 

Your website should do more than just look good. It should connect seamlessly with your operations, eliminate manual processes, and help your business scale.

Most companies use separate systems for their website, e-commerce, CRM, and accounting, forcing teams to re-enter orders, manage inventory manually, and reconcile data across platforms. This fragmentation creates inefficiencies, errors, and wasted resources that slow growth.

Using Odoo as the backbone for your website and e-commerce changes the game. In this talk, we will explain in clear business terms:

Why building websites and e-commerce on Odoo reduces friction between sales, finance, and operations while delivering a seamless customer experience.
How using Odoo allows us to design beautiful, high-converting websites without sacrificing the operational power and reporting you need to grow.
How this approach automates order management, invoicing, inventory, and customer communication directly from your website or e-commerce portal.
Why an Odoo-based architecture makes scaling your online business easier while reducing dependency on costly integrations.
How headless and advanced UI/UX strategies can still be applied while keeping Odoo as your operational core.
At Sigmagency, we experienced this first-hand. As a web agency, we built high-converting websites, but our clients struggled with fragmented tools. This led us to transition into a full-stack Odoo partner, helping SMEs connect their websites, e-commerce, and back-office processes into a single, scalable ecosystem.

Throughout this talk, we will share concrete examples of SMEs that have scaled their online services by building Odoo-powered websites connected directly to their CRM, accounting, and inventory. These examples will show how integrated ecosystems help companies sell more while working less, demonstrating the unique advantage of leveraging Odoo’s full potential.

By the end of this session, you will understand how Odoo can align your online sales channels with your operations, enabling your company to scale sustainably while improving customer satisfaction.

tracks.name: Automated Data Exports and External Integrations
tracks.speaker_line: CRETU Victor, Business Analyst at Sodexis SAS
tracks.description_html:
For Map Space Coating, data fluidity between enterprise systems and external tools is crucial for effective project management. However, the daily routine of manually filtering, exporting, and distributing data files from their ERP was tedious and prone to delays. By implementing a tailored Automated Export solution within Odoo, Map Space Coating streamlined their data extraction process.

The Challenge: Friction in Data Portability

Before standardizing their automated export process, Map Space Coating faced several operational roadblocks:
- Manual Export Fatigue: Team members had to log into Odoo daily, navigate to specific modules, apply complex filters, and manually download files.
- External Tool Bottlenecks: Project managers heavily rely on specialized external tools for advanced analysis and planning. Delays in manually exporting data from Odoo meant delays in updating these crucial external systems.
- Inconsistent Data Retrieval: Depending on who was performing the export, different filters might be accidentally applied, leading to inconsistent datasets being shared with project managers.

The Odoo Solution

To eliminate these inefficiencies, a robust, scheduled export automation was developed within Odoo. The solution was designed to act as a reliable bridge between Odoo and external tools.

1. Advanced & Flexible Filtering
- Dynamic Filter Application: The automated export engine is programmed to respect and utilize Odoo's standard, by-default filters.
- "Favorites" Integration: More importantly, the system can seamlessly draw from "Favorite" (custom-saved) filters created by users. This means project managers can define their exact data requirements once via the Odoo UI, save it as a favorite, and the automated system will apply that precise logic to all future exports.

2. Daily Automated Scheduling
To ensure data is always fresh and ready for external tools, the manual click-to-export process was completely bypassed.
- Scheduled Actions (Cron Jobs): Odoo was configured with automated scheduled actions that trigger on a daily basis.
- Zero-Touch Generation: Without any human intervention, the system runs the pre-defined queries, compiles the data, and generates the necessary export files (e.g., CSV or Excel) formatted perfectly for Map Space Coating's external tools.

3. Direct Delivery to Project Managers
Generating the file automatically is only half the solution; delivering it is the other.
- Automated Routing: Once the daily file is generated, the Odoo solution automatically drafts an email and attaches the exported file.
- Targeted Communication: The email is instantly dispatched to the specific Project Manager overseeing that data set. When the PM starts their workday, the exact data they need to import into their external tools is already waiting in their inbox.

Key Benefits and Results
The implementation of this automated export feature delivered immediate value to Map Space Coating's daily operations:
- Significant Time Savings: Administrative staff and project managers no longer waste time on repetitive manual data extraction, freeing them up for higher-value tasks.
- Guaranteed Data Consistency: By relying on saved "favorite" filters, the exported data structure remains 100% consistent every single day, preventing errors during external tool imports.
- Seamless External Integration: Project managers now have a frictionless workflow. The daily delivery of precise data files ensures their external project management and analysis tools are always up-to-date.

Conclusion
By automating the file export process in Odoo, Map Space Coating has successfully broken down data silos between their ERP and external tools. This automated, daily routine ensures that project managers are consistently equipped with the accurate, up-to-date information they need, saving time and significantly boosting overall operational efficiency.

tracks.name: Your ERP Has Data. But Not Intelligence.
tracks.speaker_line: Carlos Vazquez, CTO at INDIGO
tracks.description_html:
Many organizations invest in an ERP expecting better visibility, faster decisions, and complete control over their operations. Yet, months after implementation, leadership teams still rely on Excel exports, manual reports, disconnected dashboards, and lengthy meetings to understand what is happening in the business.

This session explores how to transform Odoo from a transactional ERP into a true operational intelligence platform. Through a live demonstration, attendees will discover how to connect sales, finance, inventory, projects, and operations into a unified decision-making environment using Odoo Spreadsheet, real-time dashboards, automation, and AI-powered insights.

Rather than focusing on reports, this talk focuses on business decisions. Participants will learn practical techniques to design executive dashboards that people actually use, identify the KPIs that matter most, and reduce dependence on spreadsheets by leveraging Odoo’s native capabilities.

The session also demonstrates how AI can enhance business visibility by identifying trends, highlighting operational risks, detecting anomalies, and helping executives make faster and better-informed decisions.

Whether you are an Odoo partner, consultant, or business leader, this presentation will provide practical ideas to help organizations move beyond simply collecting data and start turning it into operational intelligence that creates measurable business value.

tracks.name: From local complexity to global visibility: How Odoo helps international companies scale in Japan
tracks.speaker_line: Eri Nikaido & Stanislav Belooussov from Odoo
tracks.description_html:
Description:

While Japan offers immense business potential, breaking into the market presents distinct digital transformation challenges for global enterprises. Success requires harmonizing international ERP standards with Japan’s unique legal, linguistic, accounting, and logistics workflows. Through three successful Odoo implementation cases—Hachette Collections Japan, METER Japan, and Midokura Japan—this session showcases the critical role Odoo takes in bridging localized Japanese operations and global corporate management.

speakers.name: Eri Nikaido & Stanislav Belooussov
speakers.biography_html:
Eri Nikaido, Team Leader Japan at Odoo Hong Kong  

As the Indirect Team Leader, Eri spearheads Odoo’s expansion into Japan through building a robust local partner network. In 2026, Eri led a 150% increase in Odoo subscriptions in Japan. Passionate and goal-driven, she offers deep insights into pushing digital transformation with a unique localized perspective regarding Japan's distinct business culture. Drawing on 4 years of market experience, Eri offers a rare blend of global operational insight and local cultural fluency—helping Japanese businesses modernize their operations using international best practices tailored to their distinct needs.

 Stanislav Belooussov, Director of PortCities Japan K.K & Director of the Belgium Chamber of Commerce in Japan (BLCCJ)


Stanislav Belooussov is a digital transformation leader with 10 years of experience helping companies modernize their operations across Asia. As a Director at PortCities, he has supported businesses and managed teams across Japan, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore, guiding organizations through ERP implementation, process optimization, and regional expansion.

He also serves on the Board of Directors of the Belgian-Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce in Japan (BLCCJ), where he contributes to strengthening business relations between Japan and the international community. Through his work, Stanislav helps foreign companies understand the Japanese market, navigate its business environment, and successfully establish and grow their operations in Japan.

tracks.name: Streamlining Freight Management and LTL Logistics with the Sodexis FreightView Connector for Odoo v19!
tracks.speaker_line: Suganthi Karunanithi, Director Of Development at Sodexis, Inc.
tracks.description_html:
Are you frustrated with logging into multiple carrier portals, balancing scattered spreadsheets, and manually requesting individual quotes just to manage your freight and Less-Than-Truckload (LTL) shipments? Would you prefer a unified logistics environment where you can compare real-time negotiated rates, book carriers, and track bulk shipments seamlessly from your ERP?
Enter the ultimate freight consolidation platform! Managing multi-carrier freight workflows requires centralized visibility and speed. By leveraging Sodexis' specialized FreightView Shipping Connector available on the Odoo Apps Store, businesses can eliminate administrative friction entirely. With a single click from an Odoo Delivery Order, the app securely transmits package weight, classification, and volume to FreightView—instantly returning your live spot quotes, API contract rates, and LTL options into a clear, comparative list directly inside your backend.
Over the past several years, this powerful integration has transformed shipping architectures for heavy-freight and multi-company distributors. Warehouse teams can compare competing carrier costs side-by-side, instantly tender shipments, generate compliant freight labels, and schedule carrier pickups without leaving Odoo. Once booked, tracking codes, shipment numbers, and final logistics costs automatically sync back to the delivery record—facilitating accurate landed cost calculations and frictionless vendor bill reconciliation. Thousands of operational hours have been saved, giving organizations full command over their supply chain profitability.
Sodexis has been a dedicated, full-service Odoo Implementation Partner since 2012, continuously innovating its development and optimization strategies to maximize customer ROI and user experience. With extensive expertise gained over 175+ successful projects and hundreds of custom applications, Sodexis developed the FreightView Connector to seamlessly extend Odoo Enterprise environments into robust, enterprise-grade freight management systems.
Join this session to discover how the Sodexis FreightView Shipping app can eliminate your freight bottlenecks, automate complex carrier quoting, and supercharge your LTL logistics engine—and how partnering with Odoo & Sodexis plays a key role in achieving your digital transformation goals.

tracks.name: [Industry] How to manage a community care center with Odoo
tracks.speaker_line: Anissa Ratkovic, Outbound Account Executive at Odoo
tracks.description_html:
Discover Odoo Community Care: The All-in-One Solution for Healthcare and Social Services Facilities

Whether you run a care center, day center, nursing home, or short-term residential facility, your day-to-day operations are centered on people—but all too often slowed down by administrative tasks.

During this exclusive talk, our experts will introduce you to Odoo Community Care, a version of Odoo designed, configured, and tailored specifically to the unique challenges of the healthcare and social services sector.

🏥 What you’ll discover in this demo:

The Single Resident Record

Discover a highly personalized contact form to simplify the admission process. Track each resident’s journey with a dedicated summary (medical history, specific needs, emergency contacts) accessible to your teams with a single click.

Scheduling & Human Resources Management

Planning shifts for care teams can be overwhelming. Odoo automates and streamlines schedule management. Plus, centralize a comprehensive personnel directory that includes both your employees (with Full-Time Equivalent) and your volunteers.

Transparent Accounting

Streamline your financial flows with ease. On the revenue side, easily manage bed billing and track grants and subsidies. On the expense side, centralize the organization’s purchases. All of this is powered by clear and accurate cost accounting, which is essential for justifying how your budgets are allocated.
